\begin{example}[Pisot and non-Pisot Perron systems]
  \label{ex:pisot-unit-nonunit}
  The Fibonacci recurrence has characteristic polynomial
  \(X^2-X-1\), the Pell recurrence has \(X^2-2X-1\), and the
  Tribonacci recurrence has \(X^3-X^2-X-1\). Their trailing recurrence
  coefficient is \(a_0=1\), so the iterated conclusion applies. In
  ordinary base \(b\), \(U_n=b^n\) and \(a_0=b\); prime MCF-immunity
  follows, strengthening the classical fixed-base CF-immunity conclusion
  to MCF-immunity, but the unit iteration is not being asserted.

  There is also an infinite family of genuinely nonintegral weak-Perron
  systems. Let \(p,q\ge2\), put \(B=pq\), and suppose that \(B\) is not a
  square. Define
  \[
    U_{2t}=B^t,\qquad U_{2t+1}=pB^t\qquad(t\ge0).
  \]
  The successive quotients are alternately \(p\) and \(q\). Repeated
  Euclidean division in these alternating radices gives every positive
  integer a unique greedy expansion: the digit at an even position lies
  in \(\{0,\ldots,p-1\}\), and the digit at an odd position lies in
  \(\{0,\ldots,q-1\}\). Hence the LSD-first canonical language is regular,
  since a finite automaton need only track position parity, the relevant
  digit bound, and a nonzero final digit. Moreover,
  \[
    U_{n+2}=BU_n,
  \]
  and the irreducible polynomial \(X^2-B\) is the minimal recurrence
  polynomial. Its positive root \(\sqrt B\) is nonintegral and weak Perron,
  with conjugate \(-\sqrt B\) of the same modulus. The regular ray
  \(\{0^{2t}1:t\ge0\}\) has values \(B^t\). Thus \(p=2,q=3\) gives the
  sequence \(1,2,6,12,36,72,\ldots\), while \(p=2,q=5\) gives a second
  concrete member \(1,2,10,20,100,200,\ldots\).

  A genuinely nonintegral, nonunit Pisot example is obtained from
  \[
    U_0=1,\qquad U_1=3,\qquad
    U_{n+2}=2U_{n+1}+2U_n.
  \]
  If \(2<U_{n+1}/U_n\le3\), then
  \[
    \frac{U_{n+2}}{U_{n+1}}
      =2+\frac{2U_n}{U_{n+1}}\in[8/3,3),
  \]
  so induction from \(U_1/U_0=3\) proves strict increase and bounded
  quotients. The irreducible polynomial \(X^2-2X-2\) annihilates this
  nonzero rational sequence, hence is its minimal tail polynomial. Its
  dominant root is \(1+\sqrt3\), and its trailing coefficient is
  \(a_0=2\), so the action is singular modulo \(2\). Nevertheless,
  \Cref{cor:linear-perron-bounded-support-classification} shows that every
  infinite MCFL in this nonintegral system acquires unbounded prime support
  away from \(2\); singularity of the ambient action does not produce a
  valuation-only escape language.

  The polynomial \(X^2-5X+5\) gives a genuinely non-Pisot instance. Its
  dominant root \(\beta=(5+\sqrt5)/2\) is Perron, while its other conjugate
  \((5-\sqrt5)/2\) is greater than one. The integer sequence
  \[
    U_0=1,\qquad U_1=4,\qquad
    U_{n+2}=5U_{n+1}-5U_n
  \]
  begins \(1,4,15,55,200,\ldots\) and is strictly increasing. Indeed,
  \[
    U_{n+1}>3U_n>0
  \]
  holds at \(n=0\), and if it holds at \(n\), then
  \[
    U_{n+2}=5(U_{n+1}-U_n)
      >\frac{10}{3}U_{n+1}>3U_{n+1}.
  \]
  Moreover, if \(3<U_{n+1}/U_n\le4\), then
  \[
    \frac{U_{n+2}}{U_{n+1}}
      =5-\frac{5U_n}{U_{n+1}}
      \le 5-\frac54<4,
  \]
  while the lower bound was just proved; starting from \(U_1/U_0=4\)
  therefore gives \(3<U_{n+1}/U_n\le4\) for every \(n\). Thus the quotients
  are bounded, so its greedy language is the greedy language of a linear
  numeration basis with Perron recurrence in the stated sense. The
  classification below implies that every infinite MCFL in this standard
  greedy language has unbounded prime support away from \(5\).
\end{example}

\begin{theorem}[Weak-Perron radical classification]
  \label{cor:linear-perron-bounded-support-classification}
  Let \(U=(U_n)_{n\ge0}\) be a standard greedy linear numeration basis with
  \(U_0=1\), strictly increasing integer place values with bounded
  quotients, and let \(\mathcal R_U\) be the LSD-first reversal of its
  greedy representation language. Suppose that the minimal tail recurrence
  polynomial \(\mu_U\) is the minimal polynomial of a weak Perron number
  \(\beta>1\), meaning that every conjugate \(\beta'\) satisfies
  \(\abs{\beta'}\le\beta\). Let \(S_{\mathrm r}\) be the set of prime
  divisors of \(\mu_U(0)\). The residue-growth step below is a
  coefficient-level specialization of the quotient-limit mechanism in
  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; the
  prime-support/MCFL equivalence is not contained there. With this
  attribution understood, the following are equivalent:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item There exist \(k<\infty\) and an infinite \(k\)-MCFL
    \(L\subseteq\mathcal R_U\) such that
    \[
      \sup_{w\in L}\omega_{S_{\mathrm r}^c}(\val_U(w))<\infty;
    \]
    \item \(\mathcal R_U\) contains a geometric synchronized scheme whose
    values are \(cb^t\), with \(c\ge1\), \(b\ge2\);
    \item Some positive power of \(\beta\) is an integer:
    \[
      \beta^m=B\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}
      \quad\text{for some }m\ge1;
    \]
    \item For some \(m\ge1\) and \(B\ge2\),
    \[
      \mu_U(X)\mid X^m-B;
    \]
    \item For some \(m\ge1\), \(B\ge2\), and \(n_0\),
    \[
      U_{n+m}=BU_n\qquad(n\ge n_0).
    \]
  \end{enumerate}
  In the positive case, \(\mathcal R_U\) already contains the infinite
  regular ray
  \[
    \{0^{n_0+mt}1:t\ge0\},\qquad
    \val_U(0^{n_0+mt}1)=U_{n_0}B^t.
  \]
  Consequently, if no positive power of \(\beta\) is an integer, then every
  infinite MCFL \(L\subseteq\mathcal R_U\) has
  \[
    \sup_{w\in L}\omega_{S_{\mathrm r}^c}(\val_U(w))=\infty.
  \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
  The equivalence of \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} is
  \Cref{thm:bounded-outside-support-geometric-ray}.

  \input{sec_pisot_weak_perron_analysis}

  Suppose now that \textup{(ii)} holds, and write
  \[
    \val_U(W(t))=cb^t,
    \qquad \abs{W(t)}=L+Dt,
  \]
  where \(D>0\) is the total pumped length.  In a greedy \(U\)-system, a
  canonical word of length \(m\) represents a value in the half-open interval
  \([U_{m-1},U_m)\).  Hence
  \[
    U_{L+Dt-1}\le cb^t<U_{L+Dt}.
  \]
  For \(k_t=L+Dt\), the root limit gives
  \[
    U_{k_t}^{1/t}
      =\left(U_{k_t}^{1/k_t}\right)^{k_t/t}\longrightarrow\beta^D,
    \qquad
    U_{k_t-1}^{1/t}
      =\left(U_{k_t-1}^{1/(k_t-1)}\right)^{(k_t-1)/t}
       \longrightarrow\beta^D.
  \]
  Since \((cb^t)^{1/t}\to b\), taking \(t\)-th roots in the preceding
  squeeze yields \(b=\beta^D\). This is \textup{(iii)} with \(m=D\) and
  \(B=b\).

  Conditions \textup{(iii)} and \textup{(iv)} are equivalent because
  \(\beta^m=B\) says exactly that the minimal polynomial \(\mu_U\) of
  \(\beta\) divides \(X^m-B\) in \(\mathbb Q[X]\). Conditions
  \textup{(iv)} and \textup{(v)} are equivalent by the definition of
  \(\mu_U\) as the monic generator of \(I_U^{\mathrm{tail}}\): the
  divisibility \(\mu_U\mid X^m-B\) puts \(X^m-B\) in that ideal and gives
  \(U_{n+m}=BU_n\) eventually, while an eventual identity of this form
  puts \(X^m-B\) in the ideal and hence forces the divisibility.

  Finally, assume \textup{(v)} and enlarge \(n_0\), if necessary, so that
  \(n_0\ge J_{\mathrm r}\). The greedy representation of \(U_n\), in the
  LSD-first convention, is \(0^n1\). Taking
  \[
    a=0^{J_{\mathrm r}},\quad k=1,\quad
    u_1=0^{n_0-J_{\mathrm r}},\quad v_1=0^m,\quad
    w_1=s_1=\varepsilon,\quad u_2=1
  \]
  gives canonical words \(W(t)=0^{n_0+mt}1\) and
  \[
    \val_U(W(t))=U_{n_0}B^t.
  \]
  This is the asserted regular geometric ray and proves
  \textup{(v)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(ii)}. The final assertion is the
  negation of \textup{(i)}. In the strict-Perron subclass, the equality
  \(b=\beta^D\) forces every conjugate to have modulus \(\beta\) unless
  \(\beta\) has degree one; hence the theorem recovers the previous
  integral-root boundary there.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Exact open interfaces]
  \label{rem:pisot-open-interfaces}
  The terminology for linear numeration systems with Perron or Pisot
  recurrence is not uniform.
  \Cref{cor:linear-perron-prime-cf-immunity} covers the standard
  positional linear \(U\)-systems just specified, including integer
  bases, Zeckendorf/Fibonacci, Pell, higher-order Pisot recurrences, and
  non-Pisot Perron examples such as \(X^2-5X+5\).
  It asserts nothing about R\'enyi \(\beta\)-expansions, \(\beta\)-shifts,
  Parry languages, \(\beta\)-integers, Cantor real bases, or abstract
  numeration systems. Real-base systems do not in general provide the
  bijective finite-word-to-\(\mathbb N\) positional map and integral affine
  block action used here; \(\beta\)-shifts and Parry languages encode a
  dynamical admissibility problem rather than this integer-valued affine
  recurrence. Cantor real bases have nonstationary real place weights, while
  abstract numeration assigns genealogical ranks rather than values of the
  form \(\sum_j a_jU_j\). Redundant noninjective digit systems and systems
  without an eventual integral recurrence are likewise outside the stated
  hypotheses. Consequently no transfer to any of these settings is claimed.

  For a fixed nonunit recurrence witness, the ambient action can be
  singular modulo primes dividing \(a_0\), so the unrestricted unit-system
  divisibility tree need not follow. The witness-relative surviving
  statement is \Cref{thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy}: every infinite
  MCFL must acquire unbounded prime support outside that finite set or
  unbounded valuation at one of its primes. The invariant restricted
  action and the failure of arbitrary recurrence witnesses to classify
  escape behavior are distinguished in
  \Cref{prop:recurrence-witness-separation}.
  Within greedy linear numeration bases with weak-Perron recurrence, the
  residual alternative is classified by
  \Cref{cor:linear-perron-bounded-support-classification}: it occurs exactly
  when a positive power of the weak Perron number is an integer. The
  ordinary-base example preceding
  \Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain} shows that the valuation
  alternative cannot be removed.
\end{remark}

\section{A slender-context-free two-system theorem}
\label{sec:slender-cobham}

This section has a different architecture from the preceding one-system
MCFL argument. It uses a global finite cover of each full representation
language, turns every member of that cover into finitely many recurrence
sequences, and invokes finiteness of common values. In particular, none of
the finite-group return, deleted-prime, fixed-support quotient,
geometric-subsequence, or divisibility-tree arguments enters the proof.

We record the two external inputs with their hypotheses. A language \(L\)
is \emph{slender} when
\(\sup_n\#(L\cap A^n)<\infty\). In the terminology of
Ilie--Rozenberg--Salomaa, this is \(0\)-poly-slender, and a \(1\)-Dyck loop
is a language
\[
  \{u v^n w x^n y:n\ge0\}.
\]
Their Theorem~7 states that a context-free language is \(0\)-poly-slender
if and only if it is a finite union of \(1\)-Dyck loops
\cite[Theorem~7]{IlieRozenbergSalomaa2000}. The characterization was first
proved, in the equivalent terminology of iterative or semidiscrete
context-free languages, by Latteux--Thierrin
\cite{LatteuxThierrin1983}, and independently by Ilie
\cite{Ilie1994}.

Mignotte's common-value theorem concerns two rational-integer linear
recurrence sequences. We use the following precise dominant-root form. The
input consists of ordinary recurrences indexed from (0), together with
expansions
\[
  A_n=a\lambda^n+\sum_{i=2}^s P_i(n)\lambda_i^n,
  \qquad
  B_m=b\kappa^m+\sum_{j=2}^t Q_j(m)\kappa_j^m,
\]
where \(a,b\ne0\), the characteristic roots and coefficients are
algebraic, \(\lambda,\kappa>1\), and
\(
  \abs{\lambda_i}<\lambda,
  \abs{\kappa_j}<\kappa
\)
for all remaining characteristic roots. If \(\lambda\) and \(\kappa\)
are multiplicatively independent, Mignotte's proof effectively produces an
integer \(M(A,B)\) such that
\begin{equation}
  A_n=B_m,\quad n\ge M(A,B)
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  a\lambda^n=b\kappa^m.
  \label{eq:mignotte-effective-threshold}
\end{equation}
The same assertion with the sequences interchanged produces \(M(B,A)\).
In particular \(A_n=B_m\) has only finitely many nonnegative integer
solutions \cite{Mignotte1978Intersection}; Bennett--Pint\'er give an
accessible published restatement of the integral-recurrence,
unique-dominant-root hypotheses \cite{BennettPinter2015}. The qualitative
theorem below uses only finiteness. The effective refinement retains the two
thresholds in \eqref{eq:mignotte-effective-threshold}.

The next lemma supplies the hypothesis that is not a consequence merely of
the root-growth squeeze.

\begin{lemma}[Dominant-root transfer for a paired greedy loop]
  \label{lem:paired-loop-dominant-root-transfer}
  Let \(U=(U_n)_{n\ge0}\) be a strictly increasing standard greedy linear
  numeration sequence. Suppose that its least eventual recurrence
  polynomial is the minimal polynomial \(\mu\) of a weak Perron number
  \(\alpha>1\). If
  \[
    z_n=u v^n w x^n y\in\mathcal R_U\qquad(n\ge0)
  \]
  and \(D=\abs v+\abs x>0\), then there is \(h\ge1\) such that, for every
  \(0\le r<h\), the integer sequence
  \[
    Z_r(t)=\val_U(z_{ht+r})\qquad(t\ge0)
  \]
  is eventually a linear recurrence whose least eventual characteristic
  roots have the unique dominating root
  \[
    \alpha^{hD}.
  \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
  We audit the actual affine matrices. Let \(C\) be the companion matrix of
  \(\mu\). For a block \(b=b_1\cdots b_\ell\), multiplication of the digit
  matrices in \Cref{lem:affine-recurrence-block-action} gives
  \begin{equation}
    M_b=
    \begin{pmatrix}1&q_b\\0&C^\ell\end{pmatrix}
    \label{eq:paired-loop-affine-block-form}
  \end{equation}
  for a row \(q_b\), with \(M_\varepsilon=I\). Because \(\mu\) is
  irreducible over characteristic zero, it is separable, so \(C\) is
  diagonalizable over a splitting field. Hence \(C^\ell\) is
  diagonalizable even when distinct conjugates acquire the same
  \(\ell\)-th power. The eigenvalues of \(M_b\) are \(1\) and
  \(\gamma^\ell\), where \(\gamma\) runs over the conjugates of \(\alpha\).
  If \(b\ne\varepsilon\), every peripheral eigenvalue has modulus
  \(\alpha^\ell>1\), so it cannot collide with the affine eigenvalue \(1\).
  Equation \eqref{eq:paired-loop-affine-block-form} then shows that its
  peripheral generalized eigenspace is semisimple. Thus the affine row
  creates neither a peripheral eigenvalue nor a peripheral Jordan block.

  Discarding finitely many initial parameters puts the reading position
  beyond the recurrence transient. If \(v\ne\varepsilon\), the represented
  value is then a fixed scalar functional of
  \[
    M_x^n A M_v^n
  \]
  for one fixed matrix \(A\); if \(v=\varepsilon\), it is a fixed scalar
  functional of \(M_x^n A\). This follows directly by reading the five
  fixed blocks in LSD-first order; fixed initial powers used to cross the
  transient are absorbed into \(A\). Vectorization in the first case gives
  the actual powering matrix
  \[
    K=M_v^{\mathsf T}\otimes M_x,
  \]
  with the evident one-factor interpretation when one pumped block is
  empty. Its spectral radius is \(\alpha^D\). Its peripheral eigenvalues
  are exactly the products
  \(
    \gamma_1^{\abs v}\gamma_2^{\abs x}
  \)
  obtained from peripheral conjugates in the nonempty factors, and their
  generalized eigenspaces are semisimple by the preceding paragraph and
  the tensor-product Jordan formula.

  Choose \(h\) from the weak-Perron power characterization, so that
  \[
    \abs\gamma=\alpha\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \gamma^h=\alpha^h
  \]
  for every conjugate \(\gamma\). Every peripheral eigenvalue of \(K^h\) is then
  the same positive number
  \(
    \Lambda=\alpha^{hD}
  \), and the \(\Lambda\)-generalized eigenspace is still semisimple.
  All other eigenvalues of \(K^h\) have modulus strictly below
  \(\Lambda\). Cayley--Hamilton applied to the displayed scalar functional
  therefore gives, for each residue \(r\),
  \begin{equation}
    Z_r(t)=c_r\Lambda^t+
      \sum_j P_{r,j}(t)\xi_{r,j}^t,
    \qquad \abs{\xi_{r,j}}<\Lambda.
    \label{eq:paired-loop-spectral-expansion}
  \end{equation}
  This proves at matrix level that peripheral collisions coalesce to one
  algebraic root and that no polynomial factor in \(t\) can accompany it.

  It remains to audit cancellation by the actual value functional. The
  word \(z_{ht+r}\) has length \(L_r+hDt\) for a fixed \(L_r\). Greedy
  validity gives
  \[
    U_{L_r+hDt-1}\le Z_r(t)<U_{L_r+hDt}.
  \]
  The positive residue asymptotics
  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}--
  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}, applied to these two fixed
  index residues for the chosen period, show
  \[
    0<\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{Z_r(t)}{\Lambda^t}
      \le
      \limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac{Z_r(t)}{\Lambda^t}<\infty.
  \]
  In \eqref{eq:paired-loop-spectral-expansion} every lower-modulus term,
  including all its possible Jordan polynomials, is \(o(\Lambda^t)\).
  Consequently the spectral-projection coefficient \(c_r\) of the actual
  affine value functional is nonzero (indeed positive). Total peripheral
  cancellation is therefore impossible, and \(\Lambda\) survives as the
  unique dominating root of the least scalar recurrence.
\end{proof}

    =\{z\in\mathcal R_U:\val_U(z)\in X\}.

\begin{proposition}[Recurrence-witness inflation and strict separation]
  \label{prop:recurrence-witness-separation}
  If a tail has minimal recurrence polynomial \(\mu_U\), then for every
  prime \(p\) it also has a recurrence witness with characteristic
  polynomial \((X-p)\mu_U(X)\).  When \(\abs{\mu_U(0)}=1\), the trailing
  coefficient of this witness has absolute value \(p\).

  Moreover, there are two canonical eventually recurrent
  numeration systems with regular representation languages and recurrence
  witnesses whose trailing-coefficient prime set is \(\{p\}\), but with
  opposite bounded-outside-prime escape behavior:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item ordinary base \(p\) contains the infinite regular language
    \(\{0^n1:n\ge0\}\), whose values are \(p^n\);
    \item the Zeckendorf system, with \(F_0=0,F_1=1\) and
    \(F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_n\), equipped with the order-three recurrence
    witness
    \[
      F_{n+3}=-pF_n+(1-p)F_{n+1}+(p+1)F_{n+2},
    \]
    contains no infinite MCFL \(L\) for which
    \[
      \sup_{w\in L}\omega_{\{p\}^c}(\val(w))<\infty.
    \]
  \end{enumerate}
  Thus the prime divisors of an arbitrarily selected trailing coefficient
  do not determine the escape behavior of the numeration system.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
  The polynomial identity \(\mu_U(C)z_J=0\) remains valid after
  multiplication by \(X-p\).  In the companion convention, the trailing
  recurrence coefficient is the negative of the constant term of the
  characteristic polynomial, proving the first assertion.

  The base-\(p\) assertion is the preceding example.  For the Zeckendorf
  sequence, multiplication of its minimal polynomial by \(X-p\) gives
  \[
    (X-p)(X^2-X-1)
      =X^3-(p+1)X^2+(p-1)X+p,
  \]
  which is exactly the displayed recurrence and has trailing coefficient
  \(-p\).  This changes neither the sequence nor its regular canonical
  representation language.  On the other hand, its minimal recurrence
  has unit trailing coefficient.  If the displayed supremum were bounded
  by \(K\), then
  \(\omega(\val(w))\le K+1\) on \(L\), contrary to the unit-recurrence
  conclusion of
  \Cref{thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy}.  This proves the separation.
\end{proof}

Let \(E\) denote the forward shift, and let
\[
  I_U^{\mathrm{tail}}
    =\{P\in\mathbb Q[X]:P(E)U_n=0\text{ for every sufficiently large }n\}.
\]
This is an ideal of \(\mathbb Q[X]\). Let
\[
  \mu_U(X)=X^{d_{\mathrm r}}-c_{d_{\mathrm r}-1}X^{d_{\mathrm r}-1}
    -\cdots-c_1X-c_0
\]
be its monic generator, called the minimal tail recurrence polynomial.
Thus a rational polynomial annihilates some tail of \(U\) if and only if

every \(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}\), and put
\[
  S_{\mathrm r}=\{p:p\text{ is prime and }p\mid c_0\}.
\]

\begin{lemma}[Arithmetic input of Evertse]
  \label{lem:evertse-quotient-support-input}
  Let \(K\) be a number field. For \(x\in K^\times\), let \(P_K(x)\)
  be the largest norm of a finite prime ideal \(\mathfrak p\) for which
  \(\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak p}(x)\ne0\), with \(P_K(x)=1\) when
  \(x\) is a unit. If \(Z=(Z(n))_{n\ge0}\) is a nondegenerate linear
  recurrence over \(K\) whose minimal shift-annihilating polynomial has
  at least two distinct nonzero roots, then
  \[
    \lim_{\substack{r\to\infty\\ r>s\ge0,\ Z(s)\ne0}}
      P_K\!\left(\frac{Z(r)}{Z(s)}\right)=\infty.
  \]
  In particular, a rational-integer recurrence with no zero terms, all
  supported on one finite set of rational primes, cannot be both
  nondegenerate and have at least two characteristic roots.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
  The displayed uniform limit is exactly
  \cite[Theorem~3]{Evertse1984}. For the consequence, let \(S\) be the
  finite rational-prime support and choose a number field \(K\) containing
  the characteristic roots and coefficients. If \(Z(r),Z(s)\ne0\), the
  principal fractional ideal generated by \(Z(r)/Z(s)\) is supported
  only at prime ideals above primes in \(S\). Every prime ideal
  \(\mathfrak p\) above \(p\in S\) has
  \[
    \operatorname N\mathfrak p=p^{f(\mathfrak p/p)}
      \le p^{[K:\mathbb Q]}.
  \]
  Consequently
  \[
    P_K\!\left(\frac{Z(r)}{Z(s)}\right)
      \le \max\bigl(\{p^{[K:\mathbb Q]}:p\in S\}\cup\{1\}\bigr)
  \]
  for every \(r,s\) with nonzero denominator. This fixed bound
  contradicts Evertse's limit when there are at least two characteristic
  roots. Here and below, ``characteristic roots of a sequence'' always
  means the roots of its minimal shift-annihilating polynomial, not roots
  introduced by a nonminimal recurrence witness.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Injective \(S\)-unit recurrences]
  \label{lem:s-unit-increasing-recurrence-rigidity}
  Let \(Y=(Y(n))_{n\ge0}\) be a pairwise distinct sequence of positive
  rational integers satisfying a linear recurrence. If all prime
  divisors of all \(Y(n)\) belong to one finite set, then there are
  integers \(r\ge0,h\ge1,c\ge1\), and \(b\ge2\) such that
  \[
    Y(r+hn)=cb^n\qquad(n\ge0).
  \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
  Write the standard exponential-polynomial expansion, after discarding
  the contribution of the zero characteristic root and a finite initial
  segment, as
  \[
    Y(n)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(n)\alpha_i^n,
  \]
  where the \(\alpha_i\) are distinct nonzero algebraic numbers and the
  nonzero \(f_i\) are algebraic polynomials. Partition the roots by
  \(\alpha_i\sim\alpha_j\) when \(\alpha_i/\alpha_j\) is a root of
  unity. Choose \(h_0\ge1\) divisible by the orders of all such
  quotients. For each \(j\in\{0,\ldots,h_0-1\}\), substitution of
  \(n=j+h_0t\) and collection within the equivalence classes gives
  \[
    Y(j+h_0t)=\sum_C g_{C,j}(t)\beta_C^t,
    \qquad \beta_C=\alpha_i^{h_0}\quad(i\in C).
  \]
  Delete the identically zero summands. Distinct remaining \(\beta_C\)
  have quotient that is not a root of unity. Thus every residue
  subsequence is a nonzero nondegenerate recurrence; it is nonzero
  because all of its terms are positive.

  Every term of every residue subsequence is a nonzero rational integer
  supported on the prescribed finite set. If a residue subsequence had
  at least two characteristic roots, the consequence in
  \Cref{lem:evertse-quotient-support-input} would contradict the fixed
  support of all its term quotients. Hence every residue subsequence has
  exactly one characteristic root and therefore has the form
  \[
    Z(n)=f(n)\lambda^n
  \]
  with one characteristic root.

  Choose one residue subsequence and shift its index if necessary so
  that the displayed expansion holds from \(n=0\), and put
  \(e=\deg f\). Let \(E\) denote the forward shift. Over
  \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\), finite differences give
  \[
    (E-\lambda)^{e+1}Z=0,
    \qquad (E-\lambda)^eZ\ne0,
  \]
  because the \(e\)-th difference of the nonzero degree-\(e\) polynomial
  \(f\) is a nonzero constant. Hence the monic minimal shift-annihilator
  over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\) is exactly
  \((X-\lambda)^{e+1}\), and the Hankel rank of \(Z\) over that field is
  \(e+1\).

  The Hankel matrix has rational entries, and a rational matrix has the
  same rank over \(\mathbb Q\) and over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\).
  Therefore a minimal dependence among its shift columns gives a monic
  polynomial \(P\in\mathbb Q[X]\) of the same degree \(e+1\). After
  extending scalars, minimality and equality of degrees force
  \[
    P(X)=(X-\lambda)^{e+1}.
  \]
  For every
  \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q)\), the
  polynomial \(P\) is fixed and has only the root \(\lambda\); thus
  \(\sigma(\lambda)=\lambda\). Hence \(\lambda\in\mathbb Q\). Now
  \(f(n)=Z(n)/\lambda^n\in\mathbb Q\)
  for every \(n\), and interpolation from \(\deg(f)+1\) integer
  arguments gives \(f\in\mathbb Q[X]\). If \(f\) were nonconstant, clear its
  denominators to obtain a nonconstant \(g\in\mathbb Z[X]\). The
  identity \(Z(n)=f(n)\lambda^n\) would confine every prime divisor of
  every nonzero \(g(n)\) to a fixed finite set. Indeed, if
  \(\lambda=a/b\) is in lowest terms and \(g=Df\), then
  \[
    g(n)a^n=Db^nZ(n).
  \]
  Thus that fixed set is the union of the prescribed prime set and the
  prime divisors of \(Dab\). This contradicts Schur's theorem that a
  nonconstant integer polynomial has values divisible by infinitely
  many primes; see, for example, \cite{HardyWright2008}. Hence \(f\) is
  constant.

## Submission consistency check (2026-08-15)

The article's present priority narrative is consistent with this audit. It
treats the Seki weak pumping lemma, Broughan's adic classifications,
Evertse's quotient theorem, Charlier--Kreczman's residue-growth mechanism,
the fixed-base Hartmanis--Shank and Schutzenberger results, the
Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie paired-loop classification, and Mignotte's
common-value theorem as prior inputs. The retained claims are limited to the recurrence-language
combination stated with its canonical-presentation hypotheses, the
deleted-prime local rank calculation, the nonunit escape dichotomy, the
geometric-ray characterization, and the stated unit and weak-Perron
classification consequences, together with the separately proved
slender-context-free two-system theorem. The separately submitted finite-state results
remain in Supplementary Information and are compared explicitly with Shen
and Dubbe. No broader priority claim is made for fixed-base prime CF-immunity,
for arbitrary objects called Pisot numeration systems, or for the

  `10.1090/pspum/014/9985`).
- `Ilie1994`: issue `no. 2` -> `no. 1--2` (Crossref DOI
  `10.1016/0304-3975(94)00042-5`).
- `MaesRigo2002`: author order `A. Maes and M. Rigo` ->
  `M. Rigo and A. Maes` (official JALC record and DOI
  `10.25596/jalc-2002-351`).
- `LatteuxThierrin1983`: title `Semidiscrete context-free languages` ->
  `Semi-discrete context-free languages` (publisher/Crossref DOI
  `10.1080/00207168308803373`).

No intellectual claim, theorem, citation key, or citing sentence changed.
No entry was deleted: every entry has a matching index, publisher, arXiv, or
journal-archive record, so there are no deletion-related citation decisions.
No entry remains unverified.

### Audit limitations and service failures

- Crossref direct DOI resolution succeeded for all 34 DOI-bearing entries.
  Those entries were checked against Crossref as the primary index; because
  none was unavailable or empty, the protocol's OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar
  fallback was not triggered. Accordingly, cross-source redundancy was not
  achieved for every DOI-bearing entry, although title and lead-author
  identity was checked for every DOI.
- OpenAlex returned HTTP 429 for every attempted non-DOI exact-title query.
  It supplied no usable evidence for any of the 44 non-DOI entries. Each such
  entry was therefore checked using Crossref plus an official/index source
  where available, rather than Crossref plus OpenAlex.
- Semantic Scholar was also rate-limited. It succeeded only for
  `BertheGouletPerrin2025`, `MaesRigo2002`, and `Sinya2021`; it returned HTTP
  429 for `Berstel1973`, `BhowmikSuzuki2024`, `CharlierKreczman2025`,
  `CharlierRampersadRigoWaxweiler2010`, `Evertse1984`,
  `EismanRavikumar2005`, `Kitchens1998`, `Lekkerkerker1952`, `PerrinPin2004`,
  `Rigo2014Vol1`, `Yuen2022`, and `Zeckendorf1972`.
- Crossref rate-limited several later fuzzy follow-up requests after the
  direct DOI pass. The affected entries were `BhowmikSuzuki2024`,
  `CharlierKreczman2025`, `PerrinPin2004`, and `Zeckendorf1972`; their official
  arXiv, book, or zbMATH records supplied the verification instead. Service
  failures were not treated as negative evidence.

-candidate verification but witness compression: no computable bound is

-recurrence matrices. Conversely, no reduction proving undecidability is

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the
-cardinality bound in \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}, but not a
-closed bound in compact grammar-size parameters. This is a different global
-argument, not a strengthening of the weak MCFL pumping lemma.
+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and
-regular Zeckendorf results. Keeping those comparisons outside the article
-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

 \subsection{Main results}
 
-The recurrence gives an affine matrix \(D_\varepsilon\) for each digit.
-After a fixed prefix beyond the transient, concatenation is matrix
-multiplication, and every block matrix is invertible modulo each integer
-coprime to the trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
-Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami then supplies a single synchronized family
+The three principal results distinguish local information extracted from
+one pumped orbit from global information supplied by a finite cover of a
+slender language.

+\begin{maintheorem}[A: synchronized orbit and prime support]
+Let \((U,A,\mathcal R_U)\) be a canonical eventually recurrent numeration
+system with trailing recurrence coefficient \(a_0\), and let
+\(L\subseteq\mathcal R_U\) be an infinite \(k\)-MCFL. There is a fixed
+synchronized family
 \[
   W(t)=a u_1v_1^tw_1s_1^tu_2\cdots
-       u_kv_k^tw_ks_k^tu_{k+1}\qquad(t\ge0)
+       u_kv_k^tw_ks_k^tu_{k+1}\in L \qquad(t\ge0)
 \]
-inside every infinite \(k\)-MCFL. Positive pumped length makes the words
-distinct, and uniqueness of canonical representations makes
-\(N(t)=\val_U(W(t))\) pairwise distinct. For every admissible

+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete

-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the

+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.
+\]

+Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing, eventually linearly recurrent sequence
+of positive place values with a finite canonical digit language. Every
+infinite multiple context-free sublanguage contains an injective
+synchronized orbit whose values return modulo each integer coprime to the
+trailing recurrence coefficient. These returns give prime-support and

-bounded-\(\Omega\) MCF-immunity.
-
-For the minimal tail recurrence, the residual bounded-support phenomenon
-has an exact structural form. It occurs on an infinite finite-fan-out MCFL
-if and only if the canonical language contains a synchronized ray with
-values \(cb^t\). Evertse's quotient theorem is used with an explicit
-prime-ideal norm bound to reduce a fixed-support recurrence to one
-characteristic root; Schur's theorem removes its polynomial factor. The
-ratio \(b\) uses only primes dividing the minimal tail constant. In a
-standard greedy linear numeration basis with weak-Perron recurrence, residue
-asymptotics and length thresholds show that such a ray exists exactly when
-some positive power of the weak Perron number is an integer. Alternating
-radices give an infinite family with nonintegral root \(\sqrt B\) and a
-regular ray of values \(B^t\).
-
-On the promised class of valid effectively presented regular canonical
-systems, with the minimal tail recurrence and threshold supplied or
-certified, positive promised instances can be enumerated and certified. The unresolved general step is not
-candidate verification but witness compression: no computable bound is
-known for the fan-out and word lengths of a smallest geometric synchronized
-scheme. DFA path compression does not preserve the associated affine
-recurrence matrices. Conversely, no reduction proving undecidability is
-known that also preserves unique canonical representation, the minimal tail
-recurrence, and the special digit-matrix form.
-Accordingly the general decision problem remains open, while the
-weak-Perron subclass has the exact algebraic classification above.
+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the
-cardinality bound in \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}, but not a
-closed bound in compact grammar-size parameters. This is a different global
-argument, not a strengthening of the weak MCFL pumping lemma.
+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and
-regular Zeckendorf results. Keeping those comparisons outside the article
-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

+\begin{maintheorem}[A: synchronized orbit and prime support]

+  N(t+H(q))\equiv N(t)\pmod q \qquad(t\ge0).

+\begin{maintheorem}[C: slender context-free Cobham theorem]
+Let \(U\) and \(V\) be strictly increasing standard greedy linear

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs
-\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.
+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the
+scattered-set obstruction. For nonunit recurrences, an intrinsic
+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.
 
-Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu's newer substitution lemma
-\cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026} instead constrains every word
-with sufficiently many marked positions, but permits a switchable-tuple

-follows directly from that lemma. We use the older weak lemma because it
-provides exactly one fixed synchronized orbit. Placing that orbit beyond the
-recurrence transient, proving its finite-group returns, and deriving the
-prime-support consequences are the contributions here.

+The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is due to Hartmanis--Shank
+and Sch\"utzenberger \cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our

+\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}, which supplies one synchronized family.

+\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}. The substitution lemma

+size of the supported part of recurrence terms

+classifications \cite{Broughan2003}. Frougny's normalization theorem and
+the Bertrand and substitution literature provide the regular canonical
+interfaces for Pisot numeration
+\cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.

+the prime-support and MCFL classification is the additional interface
+proved here.

+For the two-system result, the paired-loop classification is due to
+Latteux--Thierrin and Ilie
+\cite{LatteuxThierrin1983,Ilie1994,IlieRozenbergSalomaa2000}, and the
+common-value input is Mignotte's theorem
+\cite{Mignotte1978Intersection}. Albayrak--Bell's quantitative
+Cobham--Semenov theorem contains the regular integer-base specialization
+and gives a stronger explicit automaton bound there
+\cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. Regular Perron-substitutive
+and regular abstract-numeration cases lie in existing Cobham theory
+\cite[Theorem~1]{Durand2011CobhamSubstitutions}%
+\cite[Theorem~49]{CharlierLeroyRigo2013CobhamANS}. The contribution of
+Main Theorem C is the passage from genuinely nonregular slender
+context-free representation languages to recurrence sequences in
+weak-Perron positional systems.

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the
-remaining decision interface.
+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.
+\]

 \begin{abstract}
-Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers that is
-eventually linearly recurrent, and suppose that a finite digit language
-gives unique representations. Combining the
-weak pumping lemma for multiple context-free languages with the affine
-recurrence action, we show that every infinite multiple context-free
-sublanguage contains one injective synchronized orbit returning
-modulo every integer coprime to the recurrence's trailing coefficient.
-Applying Broughan's standard adic classifications and our deleted-prime intrinsic
-Cantor--Bendixson calculation yields scattered-set obstructions, prime and
-bounded-\(\Omega\) MCF-immunity, and, in the unit case, quotient chains of
-arbitrary congruence depth and an induced countably branching divisibility
-tree.
-
-For the intrinsic minimal tail recurrence we prove an inverse theorem:
-bounded prime support away from its constant term occurs on an infinite
-MCFL if and only if the canonical language contains a synchronized ray
-whose values are \(cb^t\) with integers \(c\ge1\), \(b\ge2\). The
-arithmetic rigidity step is deduced explicitly from Evertse's theorem on
-prime ideals in quotients of nondegenerate recurrences. On the promised
-class of valid presentations, with a DFA and a supplied or effectively
-certified minimal tail recurrence, positive instances are semidecidable;
-the missing uniform witness bound for a general decision procedure is isolated. For

-the minimal polynomial of a weak Perron number \(\beta\), bounded support

-includes regular alternating-radix systems with nonintegral
-\(\beta=\sqrt B\). The weak-pumping mechanism still extracts only one
-synchronized orbit; it gives neither global control of the canonical

+Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing, eventually linearly recurrent sequence
+of positive place values with a finite canonical digit language. Every
+infinite multiple context-free sublanguage contains an injective
+synchronized orbit whose values return modulo each integer coprime to the
+trailing recurrence coefficient. These returns give prime-support and
+scatteredness obstructions, including MCF-immunity of the prime and

-\section{Conclusion and open interface}\label{sec:conclusion}

-The affine recurrence action turns one weak MCFL pumping family into a
-single injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Positive
-pumped length and uniqueness of canonical representation supply
-distinctness, while finite-group return times supply congruences. Applying
-Broughan's adic classifications to these orbits,
-together with the deleted-prime intrinsic derivative calculation, gives the
-scattered-set obstruction, the nonunit escape dichotomy, and prime and
-bounded-\(\Omega\) MCF-immunity.
-
-For the minimal tail recurrence, the residual bounded-support phenomenon
-has an exact structural form. It occurs on an infinite finite-fan-out MCFL
-if and only if the canonical language contains a synchronized ray with
-values \(cb^t\). Evertse's quotient theorem is used with an explicit
-prime-ideal norm bound to reduce a fixed-support recurrence to one
-characteristic root; Schur's theorem removes its polynomial factor. The
-ratio \(b\) uses only primes dividing the minimal tail constant. In a
-standard greedy linear numeration basis with weak-Perron recurrence, residue
-asymptotics and length thresholds show that such a ray exists exactly when
-some positive power of the weak Perron number is an integer. Alternating
-radices give an infinite family with nonintegral root \(\sqrt B\) and a
-regular ray of values \(B^t\).
-
-On the promised class of valid effectively presented regular canonical
-systems, with the minimal tail recurrence and threshold supplied or
-certified, positive promised instances can be enumerated and certified. The unresolved general step is not
-candidate verification but witness compression: no computable bound is
-known for the fan-out and word lengths of a smallest geometric synchronized
-scheme. DFA path compression does not preserve the associated affine
-recurrence matrices. Conversely, no reduction proving undecidability is
-known that also preserves unique canonical representation, the minimal tail
-recurrence, and the special digit-matrix form.
-Accordingly the general decision problem remains open, while the
-weak-Perron subclass has the exact algebraic classification above.
+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the
-cardinality bound in \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}, but not a
-closed bound in compact grammar-size parameters. This is a different global
-argument, not a strengthening of the weak MCFL pumping lemma.
+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and
-regular Zeckendorf results. Keeping those comparisons outside the article
-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

+\begin{maintheorem}[C: slender context-free Cobham theorem]

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs
-\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.

+The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is due to Hartmanis--Shank

+Latteux--Thierrin and Ilie

+\cite{Mignotte1978Intersection}. Albayrak--Bell's quantitative
+Cobham--Semenov theorem contains the regular integer-base specialization

The weak pumping lemma of Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami
states that an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one word that can be pumped
synchronously at \(2k\) factors \cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}. The
  lemma makes no assertion about every sufficiently long word; that
  stronger form fails for general MCFLs
  \cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.

  Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu's substitution lemma
  \cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026} is stronger in a different
  quantifier direction: after enough positions of each sufficiently long
  word are marked, it gives either a bounded pump or a factorization in
  which a tuple can be replaced by another tuple from one of finitely many
  switchable families. It does not select a single family parameterized by
  one exponent \(t\), nor does it make all replacement blocks simultaneous
  powers of fixed words. Consequently it supplies neither a fixed affine
  matrix-power expression nor a return time valid for every parameter on
  one orbit. The switchable alternative also prevents it from replacing the
  paired Ogden pump in the Zeckendorf argument above. Thus it does not by
  itself imply any immunity result proved here. We use Seki et al.'s weaker
  conclusion precisely because its one synchronized family has the fixed
  \(2k\)-block power form needed below. The imported language statement is
  only that family; its placement beyond the recurrence transient, the
  finite-group return, and all arithmetic consequences are proved here.

+Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing, eventually linearly recurrent sequence

+synchronized orbit whose values return modulo each integer coprime to the

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension

-The central inverse theorem is the geometric-ray characterization

-The difficult direction first uses local return times to pass to a

+\begin{maintheorem}[C: slender context-free Cobham theorem]
+Let \(U\) and \(V\) be strictly increasing standard greedy linear
+numeration sequences whose minimal tail recurrence polynomials are the
+minimal polynomials of weak Perron numbers \(\alpha>1\) and \(\beta>1\).
+If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are multiplicatively independent and both
+\(\operatorname{Rep}_U(X)\) and \(\operatorname{Rep}_V(X)\) are slender
+context-free languages, then \(X\) is finite.
+\end{maintheorem}
 
-There are two resolved regimes. When the trailing coefficient is a unit,
-the synchronized orbit admits quotient congruences of arbitrary prescribed
-depth and an induced copy of the countably branching divisibility tree with
-pairwise coprime, arbitrarily rough edge quotients

-A separate two-system result begins from a different language-theoretic
-input. The Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie classification gives a finite paired-loop

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs
-\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.
+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the
+scattered-set obstruction. For nonunit recurrences, an intrinsic
+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.
 
-Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu's newer substitution lemma
-\cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026} instead constrains every word
-with sufficiently many marked positions, but permits a switchable-tuple
-alternative to bounded pumping. Its substitutions are not a single
-one-parameter family of simultaneous powers of fixed blocks. They therefore
-do not give the fixed affine matrix powers, one return time for all
-parameters, or all-modulus return used here; nor do they replace the paired
-Ogden pump in the Zeckendorf argument. No immunity conclusion of this paper
-follows directly from that lemma. We use the older weak lemma because it
-provides exactly one fixed synchronized orbit. Placing that orbit beyond the
-recurrence transient, proving its finite-group returns, and deriving the
-prime-support consequences are the contributions here.
+For Main Theorem B, a bounded-support orbit is restricted to an arithmetic
+subsequence supported on a fixed finite set of primes. Its values form a
+pairwise distinct positive linear recurrence. Evertse's theorem on prime
+ideals in quotients excludes two or more characteristic roots after the
+root-of-unity classes are separated; Schur's theorem excludes a
+nonconstant polynomial factor. A further arithmetic subsequence therefore
+has values \(cb^t\). The converse is supplied by an explicit linear MCFG
+for every synchronized ray.
 
-Evertse's theorem on sums of \(S\)-units and linear recurrences is the
-nearest arithmetic input \cite{Evertse1984}. It supplies exactly the
-unbounded prime-ideal support in term quotients needed for the geometric
-rigidity step; it does not state the synchronized-language characterization.
-Later \(S\)-part estimates for recurrence terms, such as
-Bugeaud--Evertse \cite{BugeaudEvertse2017}, likewise study the size of the
-part supported on a fixed finite prime set, not synchronized numeration
-languages. The recurrence rigidity lemma below packages these classical
-arithmetic inputs for our language interface rather than claiming a separate
-new \(S\)-unit theorem. Broughan's Theorem~2.4, Corollary~3.1, and
-Theorem~4.3 \cite{Broughan2003} provide respectively the

-prime-factor strata. These ambient adic spaces and their classifications
-are standard. Our packaging consists of the MCFL-orbit application, the
-deleted-prime sets and their intrinsic derivative, and the resulting
-``local prime-factor rank.'' Proposition~2.10 is a local refinement inside
-that standard ambient space, not a new classification of it.
-Frougny's
-normalization theorem and the Bertrand and substitution literature provide
-the regular canonical interfaces for Pisot numeration
-\cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.
+In a weak-Perron greedy system, peripheral conjugates become equal after a
+common power. Residue-class asymptotics and the greedy length interval
+squeeze the geometric ratio to \(b=\beta^D\), where \(D\) is the total

-Charlier--Kreczman remove the dominant-root restriction from the regularity
-problem for positional numeration systems \cite{CharlierKreczman2025}.
-They associate a periodic alternate real base to the residue classes of the
-place-value sequence and give a full characterization of regularity through
-the graph of the greedy and quasi-greedy expansions of (1) in the shifted

-Their Proposition~10 proves that regularity of the whole greedy language

-the (p)-th powers of its dominating eigenvalues implies convergence of
-\(U_n/U_{n-p}\) to that common power when \((\lvert U_n\rvert)\) is
-eventually increasing. Under the irreducible weak-Perron hypotheses below,
-separability gives equal peripheral multiplicities, weak-Perron periodicity

-length squeeze, in essentially equivalent quotient-limit form. We retain a
-self-contained coefficient-level proof because it identifies every residue
-coefficient and verifies positivity under exactly our hypotheses. Their

+Slenderness provides global rather than local control: the

-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) retains the finite-state results: the

+The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is due to Hartmanis--Shank

+\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}, which supplies one synchronized family.

+\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}. The substitution lemma

+For the two-system result, the paired-loop classification is due to
+Latteux--Thierrin and Ilie

+common-value input is Mignotte's theorem
+\cite{Mignotte1978Intersection}. Albayrak--Bell's quantitative

+\cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. Regular Perron-substitutive
+and regular abstract-numeration cases lie in existing Cobham theory
+\cite[Theorem~1]{Durand2011CobhamSubstitutions}%
+\cite[Theorem~49]{CharlierLeroyRigo2013CobhamANS}. The contribution of
+Main Theorem C is the passage from genuinely nonregular slender
+context-free representation languages to recurrence sequences in
+weak-Perron positional systems.

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the
-remaining decision interface.
+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.
+\]

 \begin{abstract}
-Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers that is
-eventually linearly recurrent, and suppose that a finite digit language
-gives unique representations. Combining the

-recurrence action, we show that every infinite multiple context-free
-sublanguage contains one injective synchronized orbit returning
-modulo every integer coprime to the recurrence's trailing coefficient.
-Applying Broughan's standard adic classifications and our deleted-prime intrinsic
-Cantor--Bendixson calculation yields scattered-set obstructions, prime and
-bounded-\(\Omega\) MCF-immunity, and, in the unit case, quotient chains of
-arbitrary congruence depth and an induced countably branching divisibility
-tree.
-
-For the intrinsic minimal tail recurrence we prove an inverse theorem:
-bounded prime support away from its constant term occurs on an infinite
-MCFL if and only if the canonical language contains a synchronized ray
-whose values are \(cb^t\) with integers \(c\ge1\), \(b\ge2\). The

+Let \(U\) be a strictly increasing, eventually linearly recurrent sequence
+of positive place values with a finite canonical digit language. Every
+infinite multiple context-free sublanguage contains an injective
+synchronized orbit whose values return modulo each integer coprime to the
+trailing recurrence coefficient. These returns give prime-support and

-\section{Conclusion and open interface}\label{sec:conclusion}
-
-The affine recurrence action turns one weak MCFL pumping family into a
-single injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Positive
-pumped length and uniqueness of canonical representation supply
-distinctness, while finite-group return times supply congruences. Applying
-Broughan's adic classifications to these orbits,
-together with the deleted-prime intrinsic derivative calculation, gives the
-scattered-set obstruction, the nonunit escape dichotomy, and prime and
-bounded-\(\Omega\) MCF-immunity.
-
-For the minimal tail recurrence, the residual bounded-support phenomenon
-has an exact structural form. It occurs on an infinite finite-fan-out MCFL
-if and only if the canonical language contains a synchronized ray with
-values \(cb^t\). Evertse's quotient theorem is used with an explicit
-prime-ideal norm bound to reduce a fixed-support recurrence to one
-characteristic root; Schur's theorem removes its polynomial factor. The
-ratio \(b\) uses only primes dividing the minimal tail constant. In a
-standard greedy linear numeration basis with weak-Perron recurrence, residue
-asymptotics and length thresholds show that such a ray exists exactly when
-some positive power of the weak Perron number is an integer. Alternating
-radices give an infinite family with nonintegral root \(\sqrt B\) and a
-regular ray of values \(B^t\).
-
-On the promised class of valid effectively presented regular canonical
-systems, with the minimal tail recurrence and threshold supplied or
-certified, positive promised instances can be enumerated and certified. The unresolved general step is not
-candidate verification but witness compression: no computable bound is
-known for the fan-out and word lengths of a smallest geometric synchronized
-scheme. DFA path compression does not preserve the associated affine
-recurrence matrices. Conversely, no reduction proving undecidability is
-known that also preserves unique canonical representation, the minimal tail
-recurrence, and the special digit-matrix form.
-Accordingly the general decision problem remains open, while the
-weak-Perron subclass has the exact algebraic classification above.
+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the
-cardinality bound in \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}, but not a
-closed bound in compact grammar-size parameters. This is a different global
-argument, not a strengthening of the weak MCFL pumping lemma.
+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and
-regular Zeckendorf results. Keeping those comparisons outside the article
-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the
-remaining decision interface.
+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches use the passage
+\[
+  \text{structured word families}
+  \longrightarrow \text{affine matrix powers}
+  \longrightarrow \text{linear recurrences}
+  \longrightarrow \text{arithmetic rigidity}.
+\]

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie
-classification replaces a single pumped orbit by a finite paired-loop cover
-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual
-recurrence shifts, spectral data, and effective Mignotte thresholds gives the
-cardinality bound in \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}, but not a
-closed bound in compact grammar-size parameters. This is a different global
-argument, not a strengthening of the weak MCFL pumping lemma.
+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and
-regular Zeckendorf results. Keeping those comparisons outside the article
-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs
-\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.
+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the
+scattered-set obstruction. For nonunit recurrences, an intrinsic
+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.
 
-Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu's newer substitution lemma
-\cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026} instead constrains every word
-with sufficiently many marked positions, but permits a switchable-tuple

-one-parameter family of simultaneous powers of fixed blocks. They therefore
-do not give the fixed affine matrix powers, one return time for all

-Ogden pump in the Zeckendorf argument. No immunity conclusion of this paper
-follows directly from that lemma. We use the older weak lemma because it
-provides exactly one fixed synchronized orbit. Placing that orbit beyond the
-recurrence transient, proving its finite-group returns, and deriving the
-prime-support consequences are the contributions here.
+For Main Theorem B, a bounded-support orbit is restricted to an arithmetic
+subsequence supported on a fixed finite set of primes. Its values form a
+pairwise distinct positive linear recurrence. Evertse's theorem on prime
+ideals in quotients excludes two or more characteristic roots after the
+root-of-unity classes are separated; Schur's theorem excludes a
+nonconstant polynomial factor. A further arithmetic subsequence therefore

-arithmetic inputs for our language interface rather than claiming a separate

+The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is due to Hartmanis--Shank
+and Sch\"utzenberger \cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our
+language-theoretic input is the weak pumping lemma for MCFLs
+\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}, which supplies one synchronized family.
+The stronger pumping property fails for general MCFLs
+\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}. The substitution lemma
+of Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu controls every sufficiently marked long word
+but allows switchable tuples rather than one fixed simultaneous-power
+orbit \cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026}; that distinction is
+why the older weak lemma gives the matrix powers used here.
 
+Evertse's quotient theorem is the arithmetic input for the geometric-ray
+step \cite[Theorem~3]{Evertse1984}; later \(S\)-part estimates concern the
+size of the supported part of recurrence terms
+\cite{BugeaudEvertse2017}. Broughan supplies the ambient adic
+classifications \cite{Broughan2003}. Frougny's normalization theorem and
+the Bertrand and substitution literature provide the regular canonical
+interfaces for Pisot numeration
+\cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.
+Charlier--Kreczman obtain the residue-class quotient limits underlying the
+weak-Perron length squeeze \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025};
+the prime-support and MCFL classification is the additional interface
+proved here.
+
+For the two-system result, the paired-loop classification is due to
+Latteux--Thierrin and Ilie
+\cite{LatteuxThierrin1983,Ilie1994,IlieRozenbergSalomaa2000}, and the
+common-value input is Mignotte's theorem
+\cite{Mignotte1978Intersection}. Albayrak--Bell's quantitative
+Cobham--Semenov theorem contains the regular integer-base specialization
+and gives a stronger explicit automaton bound there
+\cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. Regular Perron-substitutive
+and regular abstract-numeration cases lie in existing Cobham theory
+\cite[Theorem~1]{Durand2011CobhamSubstitutions}%
+\cite[Theorem~49]{CharlierLeroyRigo2013CobhamANS}. The contribution of
+Main Theorem C is the passage from genuinely nonregular slender
+context-free representation languages to recurrence sequences in
+weak-Perron positional systems.

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension

-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping

+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility

+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.

+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.
