-For a deterministic automaton \(\mathcal A\) over the Zeckendorf digit
-alphabet, write
-\[
-  a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)
-  :=\abs{L(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal Z_m}.
-\]
-
-\begin{corollary}[Zeckendorf symmetric difference]
-  \label{cor:zeck-symmetric-diff}
-  All automata in this statement read the Zeckendorf words LSD-first, as
-  in the definition of \(\mathcal Z\) above.
-  Let \(\mathcal A\) be a deterministic automaton over the Zeckendorf
-  alphabet. Then there exists \(c_{\mathcal A,\varphi}>0\) such that
-  \[
-    \abs{(L(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal Z_m)
-         \triangle\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}
-    \ge c_{\mathcal A,\varphi}\,\frac{\varphi^m}{m}
-  \]
-  for all sufficiently large \(m\). If
-  \(a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)\) lies in the positive-density
-  alternative of \suppref{Theorem~1.18}, then along the corresponding
-  arithmetic progression of lengths one has the stronger bound
-  \(\abs{(L(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal Z_m)\triangle\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}
-  \gg \varphi^m\).
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-  Apply \suppref{Corollary~1.19} with
-  \[
-    \mathcal N=\mathcal N_{\mathrm Z},\qquad
-    \lambda=\varphi,\qquad
-    z_m=F_m,\qquad
-    T_m=\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}.
-  \]
-  The presentation hypotheses and \(z_m=F_m\) are supplied by
-  \Cref{lem:zeckendorf-canonical-presentation}; the finite-budget
-  hypothesis
-  \[
-    A_{\mathrm Z}\frac{\varphi^m}{m}
-    \le \abs{T_m}
-    \le B_{\mathrm Z}\frac{\varphi^m}{m}
-  \]
-  is \Cref{lem:zeck-prime-count}. The corollary gives the all-large-\(m\)
-  symmetric-difference bound. Its positive-density residue-class clause
-  gives the stronger \(\Omega(\varphi^m)\) bound on every residue class
-  where the limiting relative density of
-  \(L(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal Z_m\) inside \(\mathcal Z_m\) is positive.
-\end{proof}
-
-Define recall and precision for Zeckendorf slices by
-\[
-  \mathrm{Rec}_m^{(\mathrm Z)}
-  :=\frac{\abs{L(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}}
-          {\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}},
-  \qquad
-  \mathrm{Prec}_m^{(\mathrm Z)}
-  :=\frac{\abs{L(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}}
-          {a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)}
-\]
-whenever both \(\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}>0\) and
-\(a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)>0\), i.e. on lengths where the
-denominator is nonzero.
-
-\begin{corollary}[No simultaneous recall and precision in Zeckendorf]
-  \label{cor:zeck-recall-precision}
-  Let \(\mathcal A\) be a deterministic automaton over the Zeckendorf
-  alphabet. Let \(D_Z\), the constants \(c_0,\dots,c_{D_Z-1}\), and
-  \(\theta\) be supplied by
-  \Cref{lem:zeckendorf-canonical-presentation} and \suppref{Theorem~1.18}, so that
-  \[
-    \frac{a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)}{F_m}
-    =c_{m\bmod D_Z}+O(\theta^m)
-  \]
-  for all sufficiently large \(m\). Let \(B_{\mathrm Z}\) be the upper
-  estimate constant from \Cref{lem:zeck-prime-count}. For each residue
-  class \(r\bmod D_Z\), exactly one of the following alternatives holds:
-  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
-    \item If \(c_r=0\), then
-    \(\mathrm{Rec}_m^{(\mathrm Z)}\) decays exponentially along
-    \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_Z}\).
-    \item If \(c_r>0\), then there is a constant
-    \(C_{r,\varphi}>0\), for instance
-    \(C_{r,\varphi}=2C_\varphi B_{\mathrm Z}/c_r\) with
-    \(F_m\ge C_\varphi^{-1}\varphi^m\) for all large \(m\), such that
-    \[
-      \mathrm{Prec}_m^{(\mathrm Z)}\le \frac{C_{r,\varphi}}{m}
-    \]
-    for all sufficiently large \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_Z}\).
-  \end{enumerate}
-  Consequently every deterministic automaton satisfies one of the
-  following statements:
-  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
-    \item \(\mathrm{Rec}_m^{(\mathrm Z)}\) decays exponentially along
-    every residue class of lengths.
-    \item There exists at least one residue class \(r\bmod D_Z\) with
-    \(c_r>0\) such that
-    \(\mathrm{Prec}_m^{(\mathrm Z)}\le C_{\mathcal A,\varphi}/m\) for
-    all sufficiently large \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_Z}\) for which precision is
-    defined.
-  \end{enumerate}
-  Precision is left undefined on lengths with
-  \(a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)=0\); the statement makes no uniform
-  precision assertion on residue classes other than those covered by
-  the per-residue alternative.
-  Consequently no fixed DFA has both recall and precision bounded below
-  on infinitely many Zeckendorf lengths.
-\end{corollary}
-
-\begin{proof}
-  Fix \(A_{\mathrm Z},B_{\mathrm Z}>0\) as in
-  \Cref{lem:zeck-prime-count}; thus
-  \[
-    A_{\mathrm Z}\frac{\varphi^m}{m}
-    \le \abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}
-    \le B_{\mathrm Z}\frac{\varphi^m}{m}
-  \]
-  for all sufficiently large \(m\). Also fix constants
-  \(c_F',C_F'>0\) such that
-  \(c_F'\varphi^m\le F_m\le C_F'\varphi^m\) for all large \(m\).
-
-  Treat each residue class \(r\bmod D_Z\) separately. If \(c_r=0\), then
-  along \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_Z}\),
-  \(a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)=O(\theta^mF_m)\). Hence
-  \[
-    \mathrm{Rec}_m^{(\mathrm Z)}
-    \le
-    \frac{a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)}
-         {\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}}
-    \ll m\theta^m.
-  \]
-  Since \(m\theta^m=O(\theta_r^m)\) for some \(\theta_r\in(0,1)\),
-  recall decays exponentially on this residue class.
-
-  If \(c_r>0\), then for all sufficiently large \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_Z}\),
-  \[
-    a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)\ge \frac{c_r}{2}F_m
-    \ge \frac{c_rc_F'}{2}\varphi^m.
-  \]
-  Therefore
-  \[
-    \mathrm{Prec}_m^{(\mathrm Z)}
-    \le
-    \frac{\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}}
-         {a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A)}
-    \le
-    \frac{2B_{\mathrm Z}}{c_rc_F'}\cdot\frac{1}{m}.
-  \]
-  This proves the stated per-residue alternative, with
-  \(C_{r,\varphi}=2B_{\mathrm Z}/(c_rc_F')\).
-
-  If all \(c_r\) vanish, the first alternative holds on every residue
-  class, hence globally. Otherwise choose a residue class with
-  \(c_r>0\); the second alternative holds on defined lengths in that
-  arithmetic progression, and one may take
-  \(C_{\mathcal A,\varphi}=C_{r,\varphi}\).
-
-  Finally suppose that both recall and precision were bounded below by
-  some \(\delta>0\) on infinitely many Zeckendorf lengths. By the
-  pigeonhole principle, infinitely many of those lengths lie in one
-  residue class \(r\bmod D_Z\). The case \(c_r=0\) contradicts the
-  exponential recall decay above. The case \(c_r>0\) contradicts the
-  bound \(\mathrm{Prec}_m^{(\mathrm Z)}\le C_{r,\varphi}/m\) along that
-  same residue class.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{proposition}[Regular Zeckendorf slices exclude the prime scale]
-  \label{prop:zeckendorf-regular-slice-rigidity}
-  Let \(L\subseteq\mathcal Z\) be a regular language, and put
-  \[
-    \ell_m:=\abs{L\cap\mathcal Z_m}.
-  \]
-  Then there are an integer \(D_Z\ge1\), non-negative constants
-  \(c_0,\dots,c_{D_Z-1}\), and \(\theta\in(0,1)\) such that
-  \[
-    \frac{\ell_m}{F_m}=c_{m\bmod D_Z}+O(\theta^m).
-  \]
-  Consequently, on each residue class modulo \(D_Z\), the ratio
-  \[
-    \frac{\ell_m}{\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}}
-  \]
-  either tends to \(0\) exponentially up to the harmless polynomial
-  factor \(m\), or tends to \(+\infty\) at least linearly in \(m\).
-  In particular no regular sublanguage of \(\mathcal Z\) has
-  \(\ell_m=\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}\) for all sufficiently
-  large \(m\).
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-  Let \(\mathcal A\) be a deterministic automaton recognizing \(L\).
-  Since \(L\subseteq\mathcal Z\), one has
-  \[
-    \ell_m=\abs{L(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal Z_m}
-          =a_m^{(\mathrm Z)}(\mathcal A).
-  \]
-  By \Cref{lem:zeckendorf-canonical-presentation}, the canonical
-  Zeckendorf presentation is trim, deterministic, strongly connected,
-  has Perron root \(\varphi\), and satisfies
-  \(z_m=\abs{\mathcal Z_m}=F_m\). Applying
-  the background relative-density theorem
-  \suppref{Theorem~1.18} to this presentation and to
-  \(\mathcal A\) gives the displayed expansion; its proof is the
-  substochastic product expansion of
-  \suppref{Lemma~1.17} combined with the positive
-  periodic denominator constants from \suppref{Lemma~1.16}.
-
-  Fix a residue class \(r\bmod D_Z\). By \Cref{lem:zeck-prime-count}
-  there are constants \(A_{\mathrm Z},B_{\mathrm Z}>0\) such that
-  \[
-    A_{\mathrm Z}\frac{\varphi^m}{m}
-    \le\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}
-    \le B_{\mathrm Z}\frac{\varphi^m}{m}
-  \]
-  for all sufficiently large \(m\). Also fix \(c_F'',C_F''>0\) such that
-  \(c_F''\varphi^m\le F_m\le C_F''\varphi^m\) for all large \(m\).
-
-  If \(c_r=0\), then along \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_Z}\) we have
-  \[
-    \ell_m=O(\theta^mF_m)=O(\theta^m\varphi^m).
-  \]
-  Hence
-  \[
-    \frac{\ell_m}{\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}}
-    =O(m\theta^m),
-  \]
-  which tends to \(0\) exponentially after increasing \(\theta\) within
-  \((0,1)\).
-
-  If \(c_r>0\), then for all sufficiently large
-  \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_Z}\),
-  \[
-    \ell_m\ge\frac{c_r}{2}F_m
-        \ge\frac{c_rc_F''}{2}\varphi^m.
-  \]
-  Therefore
-  \[
-    \frac{\ell_m}{\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}}
-    \ge
-    \frac{c_rc_F''}{2B_{\mathrm Z}}\,m,
-  \]
-  and the ratio tends to \(+\infty\) at least linearly on this residue
-  class.
-
-  Every residue class falls into exactly one of these two cases. Thus
-  equality
-  \(\ell_m=\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}}\) cannot hold for all
-  sufficiently large \(m\), since any fixed residue class contains
-  arbitrarily large lengths and on that class the ratio cannot remain
-  equal to \(1\).
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{corollary}[Prime Zeckendorf language is not regular]
-  \label{cor:zeckendorf-prime-language-not-regular}
-  The prime Zeckendorf language \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal Z}\) is not
-  regular.
-\end{corollary}
-
-This corollary is now an immediate consequence of the stronger
-PNT-free regular-immunity theorem. The preceding
-\Cref{prop:zeckendorf-regular-slice-rigidity} remains useful as a
-separate slice-scale obstruction: it explains why the exact
-prime-slice cardinalities cannot be reproduced by a regular
-sublanguage on all large lengths. General results relating
-\(S\)-recognizability, \(S\)-automaticity, and morphic predicates in
-abstract numeration systems include Maes--Rigo \cite{MaesRigo2002} and
-the standard accounts \cite{AlloucheShallit2003,Rigo2014Vol1,Rigo2014Vol2}.
-
-\begin{proof}
-  This follows at once from
-  \Cref{cor:zeckendorf-prime-language-reg-immune}, since an infinite
-  regular language is an infinite regular sublanguage of itself.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{remark}[Sofic corollary]
-  \label{rem:zeckendorf-primes-not-sofic}
-  The preceding non-regularity statement excludes eventual sofic
-  realization of the prime Zeckendorf length slices by the following
-  short argument.
-  Let \(\mathcal B_m(X)\) denote the admissible words of length
-  \(m\) in a sofic shift \(X\). If
-  \(\mathcal B_m(X)=\mathcal P_m^{(\mathrm Z)}\) for all \(m\ge N\),
-  then
-  \[
-    \mathcal B(X)\triangle\mathcal P_{\mathcal Z}\subseteq \{0,1\}^{<N},
-  \]
-  a finite set. Since \(\mathcal B(X)\) is regular
-  (\cite[Theorem~3.2.1]{LindMarcus1995}; see also
-  \cite[Chapter~4]{PerrinPin2004}), this would make
-  \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal Z}\) a finite symmetric difference away from a
-  regular language, hence regular itself, contradicting
-  \Cref{cor:zeckendorf-prime-language-not-regular}.
-\end{remark}

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence â‰  evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter â‰  compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion â‰  excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
âœ… [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
âŒ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
âœ… Write â†’ Run (pass) â†’ Revert fix â†’ Run (MUST FAIL) â†’ Restore â†’ Run (pass)
âŒ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
âœ… [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
âŒ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
âœ… Re-read plan â†’ Create checklist â†’ Verify each â†’ Report gaps or completion
âŒ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
âœ… Agent reports success â†’ Check VCS diff â†’ Verify changes â†’ Report actual state
âŒ Trust agent report
```

## Why This Matters

From 24 failure memories:
- your human partner said "I don't believe you" - trust broken
- Undefined functions shipped - would crash
- Missing requirements shipped - incomplete features
- Time wasted on false completion â†’ redirect â†’ rework
- Violates: "Honesty is a core value. If you lie, you'll be replaced."

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

## The Bottom Line

**No shortcuts for verification.**

Run the command. Read the output. THEN claim the result.

This is non-negotiable.

+\input{preamble}
+
+\title[Finite-state prime slices]{Finite-state prime slices in positional and Zeckendorf numeration}
+
+\author{Haobo Ma}
+\address[Haobo Ma]{AELF PTE LTD., \#14-02, Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 1, 8 Marina Blvd, Singapore 018981}
+\email[Haobo Ma]{auric@aelf.io}
+
+\author{Wenlin Zhang}
+\address[Wenlin Zhang]{National University of Singapore, Singapore}
+\email[Wenlin Zhang]{e1327962@u.nus.edu}
+\thanks{Corresponding author: Wenlin Zhang.}
+
+\date{}
+
+\begin{document}
+
+\begin{abstract}
+We study prime-valued slices of regular positional languages through the
+transition matrices of a fixed deterministic finite automaton. In ordinary
+integer bases, spectral decomposition gives a density dichotomy and
+effective bounds for prime slices with the automaton held fixed. The same
+matrix framework yields word-growth asymptotics needed for finite-budget
+estimates. For Zeckendorf representations, a unimodular block action and
+the canonical Fibonacci intervals give corresponding regular-language
+growth and prime-support obstructions. We compare these fixed-automaton
+estimates with qualitative nonrecognizability results and with bounds that
+allow state complexity to grow, and record the analytic prime estimates
+used in the comparison.
+\end{abstract}
+
+\subjclass[2020]{68Q45, 11A63, 11B39}
+\keywords{finite automata, prime numbers, positional numeration, Zeckendorf representation, regular languages}
+
+\maketitle
+
+\section*{Introduction}
+
+A regular language turns positional counting into a finite-dimensional
+matrix problem. Powers of its transition matrix separate transient states,
+periodic recurrent components, and the spectral terms that control word
+counts in arithmetic length classes. Coupling those counts with prime
+estimates gives quantitative information for a fixed automaton rather than
+only a recognition obstruction.
+
+The first part develops this transition-matrix analysis for ordinary bases
+and proves the resulting density and prime-slice alternatives. The second
+part treats Zeckendorf representations, where Fibonacci length intervals
+and a unimodular digit action replace constant-base scaling. The final
+appendix collects the analytic comparisons used by both branches. All
+constants are attached to the displayed automaton and recurrence data.
+

+\input{sec_zeckendorf}

+\input{sec_analytic}

+\end{document}

+\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
 
-The nearest broader global problem is the degeneracy/Cobham-extension
-problem for context-free sequences discussed by Caucal and Le Gonidec
-\cite{CaucalLeGonidec2014}; this paper does not settle it. The weak pumping
-mechanism itself still supplies only one ray inside one infinite MCFL, and
-two representations of the same set may supply unrelated rays with no
-common values. It neither controls every sufficiently long word nor the
-whole canonical language. The slender-context-free theorem proved here
-escapes that ceiling only because the Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie

-of each full representation language. Mignotte's theorem then makes every
-pair of loop images have finite intersection. Retaining the individual

+The affine recurrence action converts one synchronized pumping family into
+an injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Adic topology
+turns those returns into scatteredness and prime-support obstructions, while
+Evertse's quotient theorem and Schur's theorem identify the remaining
+bounded-support possibility as a geometric ray \(cb^t\). In standard
+weak-Perron greedy systems, the length squeeze classifies that possibility
+algebraically: it occurs if and only if a positive power of the weak Perron
+root is an integer.
 
-The Supplementary Information (Online Resource 1) contains the independent fixed-DFA density and

-leaves the main theorem chain centered on synchronized recurrence orbits
-and their arithmetic consequences.
+For slender context-free languages, a finite paired-loop cover supplies
+global control of every represented value. The same affine evaluation sends
+each loop to finitely many recurrence sequences, and dominant-root transfer
+followed by Mignotte's theorem gives the two-system Cobham finiteness result.
+Complete recurrence and loop data yield an effective cardinality bound. For
+the one-system geometric-ray problem, candidate verification is effective,
+but no uniform bound is known for the fan-out and block lengths of a smallest
+witness; this is the missing step toward a general decision procedure.

-undecidability for unrestricted matrix equations does not preserve the

+\subsection{Proof architecture}
 
-There are two resolved regimes. When the trailing coefficient is a unit,
-the synchronized orbit admits quotient congruences of arbitrary prescribed
-depth and an induced copy of the countably branching divisibility tree with
-pairwise coprime, arbitrarily rough edge quotients
-(\Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain,thm:unit-mcfl-divisibility-tree}).
-For standard greedy linear numeration bases with weak-Perron recurrence,
-length thresholds complete the bounded-support classification: the
-geometric-ray properties above hold exactly when some positive power of the
-weak Perron number is an integer
-(\Cref{cor:linear-perron-bounded-support-classification}). Hence the
-strict-Perron subclass recovers the integral-root boundary, while
-imprimitive examples such as alternating-radix systems with
-\(\beta=\sqrt B\) give genuinely nonintegral positive cases. The
-residue-growth mechanism used in this specialization is not new:
-Charlier--Kreczman obtain residue-class quotient limits for regular
-positional systems and record the corresponding converse for eventually
-increasing linear recurrences whose dominating eigenvalues have a common
-power \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}. Our
-contribution here is the prime-support/MCFL interface and its exact
-geometric-ray and algebraic classification, not that quotient-limit
-mechanism.
+The recurrence first becomes a finite-dimensional affine action. After a
+prefix beyond the recurrence transient, every digit acts by an integral
+matrix, and every block matrix is invertible modulo integers coprime to the
+trailing coefficient. The weak pumping lemma of
+Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami supplies one family in which finitely many
+fixed blocks are raised to a common exponent. A common order of their
+matrices in a finite general linear group gives the returns in Main
+Theorem A; positive pumped length and canonical uniqueness give
+distinctness.
 
-A separate two-system result begins from a different language-theoretic
-input. The Latteux--Thierrin--Ilie classification gives a finite paired-loop
-cover of an entire slender context-free language. Combining that global
-cover with the affine block action, the weak-Perron residue asymptotics, and
-Mignotte's common-value theorem for recurrence sequences yields
-\Cref{thm:slender-cfl-cobham}. Thus, for two multiplicatively independent
-weak-Perron linear numeration systems, the representations of one fixed set
-cannot both be slender context-free unless the set is finite. The natural
-published benchmark for the regular integer-base case is Albayrak--Bell's
-\(d\)-dimensional quantitative Cobham--Semenov theorem for sparse automatic
-sets \cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. It contains the regular
-integer-base specialization, covers regular sparse (in particular regular
-poly-slender) tuple languages more broadly, and supplies an explicit
-automaton-data bound. Regular Perron-substitutive and regular abstract-
-numeration shadows likewise belong to existing Cobham theory
-\cite[Theorem~1]{Durand2011CobhamSubstitutions}%
-\cite[Theorem~49]{CharlierLeroyRigo2013CobhamANS}. The new part here is the
-passage from regular recognition to full slender context-free representation
-languages, together with the dominant-root transfer for paired loops in
-weak-Perron positional systems. This is not an extension of the one-orbit
-pumping theorem: it does not use finite-group returns, deleted-prime
-topology, fixed-support quotient rigidity, geometric subsequences, or the
-divisibility tree. From complete effective recurrence data and constructive
-paired-loop covers, \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality} additionally
-computes a cardinality bound. It does not extract an Albayrak--Bell-style
-closed formula in compact grammar-size parameters.
+These local returns place the orbit densely in the relevant congruence
+neighbourhoods. Broughan's adic classifications then yield the
+scattered-set obstruction. For nonunit recurrences, an intrinsic
+Cantor--Bendixson calculation after deleting the exceptional primes gives
+the alternative between new prime divisors and increasing exceptional
+valuations. In the unit case, the same returns also produce quotient
+congruences of arbitrary depth and a divisibility tree.
 
-\subsection{Relation to prior work}\label{subsec:prior-work}
+For Main Theorem B, a bounded-support orbit is restricted to an arithmetic
+subsequence supported on a fixed finite set of primes. Its values form a
+pairwise distinct positive linear recurrence. Evertse's theorem on prime
+ideals in quotients excludes two or more characteristic roots after the
+root-of-unity classes are separated; Schur's theorem excludes a
+nonconstant polynomial factor. A further arithmetic subsequence therefore
+has values \(cb^t\). The converse is supplied by an explicit linear MCFG
+for every synchronized ray.
 
-The fixed-base context-free prime obstruction is classical, due to
-Hartmanis--Shank and Sch\"utzenberger
-\cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. Our language-theoretic input
-is exactly Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami's weak pumping lemma
-\cite[Lemma~3.2]{SekiEtAl1991}: an infinite \(k\)-MCFL contains one family
-with \(2k\) fixed factors pumped by the same exponent. It says nothing
-about every sufficiently long word, and the corresponding strong pumping
-property fails for general MCFLs
-\cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}.
+In a weak-Perron greedy system, peripheral conjugates become equal after a
+common power. Residue-class asymptotics and the greedy length interval
+squeeze the geometric ratio to \(b=\beta^D\), where \(D\) is the total
+pumped length. This proves the algebraic classification in Main Theorem B
+without assuming that the full greedy language is regular.
 
-Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Lyu's newer substitution lemma
-\cite[Theorem~4.5]{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026} instead constrains every word
-with sufficiently many marked positions, but permits a switchable-tuple
-alternative to bounded pumping. Its substitutions are not a single
-one-parameter family of simultaneous powers of fixed blocks. They therefore
-do not give the fixed affine matrix powers, one return time for all
-parameters, or all-modulus return used here; nor do they replace the paired
-Ogden pump in the Zeckendorf argument. No immunity conclusion of this paper
-follows directly from that lemma. We use the older weak lemma because it
-provides exactly one fixed synchronized orbit. Placing that orbit beyond the
-recurrence transient, proving its finite-group returns, and deriving the
-prime-support consequences are the contributions here.
+Slenderness provides global rather than local control: a classical
+classification covers an entire slender context-free language by finitely
+many paired loops. The affine action
+turns each loop, after finitely many residue restrictions, into recurrence
+sequences with one positive dominant root. Mignotte's theorem makes the
+common-value set of a loop from the \(U\)-cover and a loop from the
+\(V\)-cover finite, proving Main Theorem C.
 
-Evertse's theorem on sums of \(S\)-units and linear recurrences is the
-nearest arithmetic input \cite{Evertse1984}. It supplies exactly the
-unbounded prime-ideal support in term quotients needed for the geometric
-rigidity step; it does not state the synchronized-language characterization.
-Later \(S\)-part estimates for recurrence terms, such as
-Bugeaud--Evertse \cite{BugeaudEvertse2017}, likewise study the size of the
-part supported on a fixed finite prime set, not synchronized numeration
-languages. The recurrence rigidity lemma below packages these classical
-arithmetic inputs for our language interface rather than claiming a separate
-new \(S\)-unit theorem. Broughan's Theorem~2.4, Corollary~3.1, and
-Theorem~4.3 \cite{Broughan2003} provide respectively the
-\(\mathbb Q\)-space classification, Cantor completion, and full-adic
-prime-factor strata. These ambient adic spaces and their classifications
-are standard. Our packaging consists of the MCFL-orbit application, the
-deleted-prime sets and their intrinsic derivative, and the resulting
-``local prime-factor rank.'' Proposition~2.10 is a local refinement inside
-that standard ambient space, not a new classification of it.
-Frougny's
-normalization theorem and the Bertrand and substitution literature provide
-the regular canonical interfaces for Pisot numeration
-\cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.
+\subsection{Relation to prior work}
 
-Charlier--Kreczman remove the dominant-root restriction from the regularity
-problem for positional numeration systems \cite{CharlierKreczman2025}.
-They associate a periodic alternate real base to the residue classes of the
-place-value sequence and give a full characterization of regularity through
-the graph of the greedy and quasi-greedy expansions of (1) in the shifted
-alternate bases. Their procedure is a semidecision in general, and becomes a
-decision procedure when the associated alternate base is known to be Parry.
-Their Proposition~10 proves that regularity of the whole greedy language
-forces residue-class consecutive-quotient limits. More directly relevant
-here, Remark~12 states that, for an arbitrary linear recurrence, equality of
-the (p)-th powers of its dominating eigenvalues implies convergence of
-\(U_n/U_{n-p}\) to that common power when \((\lvert U_n\rvert)\) is
-eventually increasing. Under the irreducible weak-Perron hypotheses below,
-separability gives equal peripheral multiplicities, weak-Perron periodicity
-gives the common power, and strict increase supplies their last hypothesis.
-Thus their work already contains the root-growth mechanism needed for our
-length squeeze, in essentially equivalent quotient-limit form. We retain a
-self-contained coefficient-level proof because it identifies every residue
-coefficient and verifies positivity under exactly our hypotheses. Their
-regularity characterization neither assumes nor concludes anything about
-MCFL sublanguages, bounded prime support, synchronized geometric schemes, or
-the five equivalent conditions proved here; conversely, our theorem does not
-characterize regularity of the whole greedy language.

 \subsection{Organization}
 
-\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} begins with the context-free Zeckendorf
-motivation, develops the recurrent block action and synchronized MCFL orbit,
-proves the local-adic and prime-support consequences, establishes the
-geometric-ray characterization and its effective boundary, and concludes
-with the unit and weak-Perron specializations. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham}
-uses the global paired-loop classification to prove the separate two-system
-finiteness theorem, gives its effective cardinality refinement from complete
-presentations, and locates its nonregular contribution relative to existing
-Cobham results. \Cref{sec:conclusion} summarizes the proved scope and the
-remaining decision interface.
+\Cref{sec:context-free-pisot} develops local rigidity from one synchronized
+orbit: the Zeckendorf model, affine recurrence action, prime-support
+obstructions, geometric-ray characterization, and weak-Perron
+classification. \Cref{sec:slender-cobham} develops global rigidity from a
+finite paired-loop cover and proves the two-system theorem and its effective
+cardinality refinement. Both branches pass from structured word families to
+affine matrix powers, then to linear recurrences and arithmetic rigidity.

+\begin{remark}[Scope]
   \label{rem:pisot-open-interfaces}
-  The terminology for linear numeration systems with Perron or Pisot
-  recurrence is not uniform.
-  \Cref{cor:linear-perron-prime-cf-immunity} covers the standard
-  positional linear \(U\)-systems just specified, including integer
-  bases, Zeckendorf/Fibonacci, Pell, higher-order Pisot recurrences, and
-  non-Pisot Perron examples such as \(X^2-5X+5\).
-  It asserts nothing about R\'enyi \(\beta\)-expansions, \(\beta\)-shifts,
-  Parry languages, \(\beta\)-integers, Cantor real bases, or abstract
-  numeration systems. Real-base systems do not in general provide the
-  bijective finite-word-to-\(\mathbb N\) positional map and integral affine
-  block action used here; \(\beta\)-shifts and Parry languages encode a
-  dynamical admissibility problem rather than this integer-valued affine
-  recurrence. Cantor real bases have nonstationary real place weights, while
-  abstract numeration assigns genealogical ranks rather than values of the
-  form \(\sum_j a_jU_j\). Redundant noninjective digit systems and systems
-  without an eventual integral recurrence are likewise outside the stated
-  hypotheses. Consequently no transfer to any of these settings is claimed.
-
-  For a fixed nonunit recurrence witness, the ambient action can be
-  singular modulo primes dividing \(a_0\), so the unrestricted unit-system
-  divisibility tree need not follow. The witness-relative surviving
-  statement is \Cref{thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy}: every infinite
-  MCFL must acquire unbounded prime support outside that finite set or
-  unbounded valuation at one of its primes. The invariant restricted
-  action and the failure of arbitrary recurrence witnesses to classify
-  escape behavior are distinguished in
-  \Cref{prop:recurrence-witness-separation}.
-  Within greedy linear numeration bases with weak-Perron recurrence, the
-  residual alternative is classified by
-  \Cref{cor:linear-perron-bounded-support-classification}: it occurs exactly
-  when a positive power of the weak Perron number is an integer. The
-  ordinary-base example preceding
-  \Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain} shows that the valuation
-  alternative cannot be removed.
+  The results concern integer-valued greedy linear numeration with an
+  eventual integral recurrence. Real-base dynamical expansions and
+  genealogical-rank abstract numeration use different evaluation maps. For
+  a nonunit recurrence witness, \Cref{thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy}
+  retains the alternative between new primes and increasing valuations;
+  within the weak-Perron greedy subclass,
+  \Cref{cor:linear-perron-bounded-support-classification} identifies the
+  latter bounded-support regime by integrality of a positive power of the
+  dominant root.
 \end{remark}

-\begin{remark}[Priority and scope]
+\begin{remark}[Cobham comparison]
   \label{rem:slender-cobham-priority}
-  Three existing Cobham statements delimit the result. The natural published
-  benchmark for the regular integer-base case is the quantitative
-  Cobham--Semenov theorem of Albayrak--Bell. For multiplicatively independent
-  integers \(k,\ell\ge2\), they prove that the intersection of a sparse
-  \(k\)-automatic subset of \(\mathbb N^d\) and a sparse \(\ell\)-automatic
-  subset of \(\mathbb N^d\) is finite, with an explicit bound in terms of the
-  bases, dimension, and minimal automata
-  \cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. Taking the two sets equal gives
-  simultaneous sparse automatic finiteness. A slender regular integer-base
-  representation language is sparse, so this contains the regular
-  integer-base specialization of the theorem above. More broadly, their
-  \(d\)-dimensional statement covers sparse automatic tuple sets whose regular
-  representation languages may have polynomial rather than bounded word
-  growth; in particular it covers the regular poly-slender integer-base
-  shadow. Their theorem is strictly stronger on the overlap and broader in
-  this regular direction. The effective result above computes a cardinality
-  bound from the complete recurrence and paired-loop data, but it does not
-  close the quantitative gap: Albayrak--Bell give a closed expression in the
-  bases, dimension, and numbers of states of the minimal automata. They also
-  distinguish that cardinality estimate from the separate task of actually
-  computing the intersection; we make the same distinction here.
+  In regular integer bases, Albayrak--Bell's quantitative Cobham--Semenov
+  theorem contains the slender specialization above and extends to sparse
+  automatic tuple sets of polynomial growth
+  \cite[Theorems~1.1 and 4.1]{AlbayrakBell2023}. Their result is stronger on
+  this overlap: its bound is an explicit expression in the bases, dimension,
+  and minimal-automaton sizes, whereas \Cref{thm:effective-slender-cfl-cardinality}
+  computes a bound from complete recurrence and paired-loop data.
 
-  Second, Durand proves that a sequence which is simultaneously
-  \(\alpha\)- and \(\beta\)-substitutive for multiplicatively independent
-  Perron numbers is ultimately periodic
-  \cite[Theorem~1]{Durand2011CobhamSubstitutions}. Third, the abstract-
-  numeration theorem of Charlier--Leroy--Rigo starts with infinite regular
-  languages ordered genealogically, requires both representation languages
-  of the set to be regular, and concludes that simultaneous recognition in
-  two independent systems gives a finite union of arithmetic progressions
-  \cite[Definitions~33, 34, and 47 and Theorem~49]%
-  {CharlierLeroyRigo2013CobhamANS}. In its exponential case, independence
-  means multiplicative independence of the dominant language-growth
-  eigenvalues. Thus the regular Perron-substitutive and regular abstract-
-  numeration shadows are already part of existing Cobham theory.
-
-  Those recognition hypotheses fail at the full scope of the theorem above.
-  A slender context-free representation language may be genuinely
-  nonregular, so it need not furnish either a finite automaton recognizing
-  the full representation language or a substitutive characteristic
-  sequence. The dimension in Albayrak--Bell does not remove this condition:
-  a coordinate or product encoding enters their theorem only when its padded
-  synchronous tuple language is itself sparse regular, and its coordinates
-  still use ordinary integer-base valuation. It therefore does not absorb a
-  genuinely nonregular paired-loop language or replace the weak-Perron affine
-  value map used here. Nor need a weak-Perron positional system supply the
-  regular canonical, genealogical-rank interface required by an abstract
-  numeration system.
-  The role of \Cref{lem:paired-loop-dominant-root-transfer} is precisely the
-  nonregular weak-Perron bridge: it sends each word-theoretic paired loop to
-  residue subsequences with a unique positive dominant root, while resolving
-  peripheral collisions, affine and tensor-product Jordan factors, and
-  cancellation by the value functional. Only after that transfer can
-  Mignotte's common-value theorem be applied.
-
-  Accordingly, the regular integer-base and regular abstract-numeration
-  shadows belong to existing Cobham theory. What is new here is the passage
-  from regular recognition to full slender context-free representation
-  languages, together with the dominant-root transfer for paired loops in
-  weak-Perron positional systems. This claim does not extend to nonregular
-  poly-slender representation languages: finite unions of higher Dyck loops
-  would require a genuinely multivariate argument, which is not asserted
-  here.
+  The new passage is from a possibly nonregular slender context-free
+  representation language to residue subsequences with one positive
+  dominant root in a weak-Perron positional system. The regular
+  Perron-substitutive and genealogically ordered abstract-numeration cases

-  theorem for Euler products with non-negative integral exponents
-  \cite{Estermann1928}; see also the P\'olya--Carlson formulation
-  \cite{Polya1923,Carlson1921}. Under the displayed hypotheses,
-  infinitely many prime-indexed primitive factors occur with positive
-  exponent, so Estermann's theorem applies directly.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{proposition}[Classical determinant comparison]
-  \label{prop:finite-zeta-imaginary-periodicity}
-  If \(M\) is a finite square complex matrix, the scalar determinant
-  model, with scalar exponential multiplying the matrix,
-  \[
-    F_M(s):=\det(I-(e^{-s})M)^{-1}
-  \]
-  is \(2\pi i\)-periodic wherever it is holomorphic. Therefore it
-  cannot agree on a non-empty right-half-plane open set with a
-  nonconstant ordinary Dirichlet series such as the Riemann
-  \(\zeta\)-function.
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-  The periodicity is the identity
-  \[
-    F_M(s+2\pi i)
-    =\det(I-(e^{-(s+2\pi i)})M)^{-1}
-    =F_M(s).
-  \]
-  If \(F(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}\) is an ordinary Dirichlet series with
-  some non-zero coefficient at \(n\ge2\), then
-  \[
-    G(s):=F(s+2\pi i)-F(s)
-      =\sum_{n\ge1}a_n(e^{-2\pi i\log n}-1)n^{-s}
-  \]
-  has a non-zero first coefficient, where \(\log\) is the real
-  logarithm. The usual uniqueness lemma for ordinary Dirichlet series,
-  obtained by multiplying by the first index to the power \(\sigma\)
-  and letting \(\sigma\to+\infty\), gives \(G(\sigma)\ne0\) for all
-  sufficiently large real \(\sigma\). Thus \(F\) is not
-  \(2\pi i\)-periodic, and the identity theorem prevents agreement with
-  a scalar determinant model on such an open set.
-\end{proof}

-\section{Deterministic Automata and Base-\texorpdfstring{$b$}{b} Primes}
-\label{sec:automata}
-
-Throughout this section, fix an integer \(b\ge 2\) and write
-\(\Sigma_b:=\{0,1,\dots,b-1\}\).
-
-\begin{definition}\label{def:dfa}
-A complete deterministic finite automaton over \(\Sigma_b\) is a tuple
-\(\mathcal A=(Q,\Sigma_b,\delta,q_0,F)\), where \(Q\) is a finite state
-set, \(q_0\in Q\) is the initial state, \(F\subseteq Q\) is the set of
-accepting states, and
-\[
-  \delta:Q\times\Sigma_b\to Q
-\]
-is a total transition map.
-\end{definition}
-
-Completeness is only a convenient normalization here: adjoining a sink
-state completes any DFA without changing its language. The substantive
-restriction throughout is determinism.
-
-For \(m\ge 0\), write
-\[
-  a_m(\mathcal A)
-  :=\#\{w\in\Sigma_b^m:\mathcal A\text{ accepts }w\}.
-\]
-
-\begin{theorem}[Density dichotomy for DFA languages]
-  \label{thm:dfa-density-dichotomy}
-  There exist an integer \(D_A\ge 1\), non-negative constants
-  \(c_0,\dots,c_{D_A-1}\), and \(\theta\in(0,1)\) such that
-  \[
-    \frac{a_m(\mathcal A)}{b^m}=c_{m\bmod D_A}+O(\theta^m)
-    \qquad (m\to\infty).
-  \]
-  Consequently exactly one of the following alternatives holds:
-  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
-    \item There exists \(\eta\in(0,1)\) such that the normalized
-    density satisfies
-    \[
-      \frac{a_m(\mathcal A)}{b^m}=O(\eta^m);
-    \]
-    equivalently, \(a_m(\mathcal A)=O((b\eta)^m)\).
-    \item There exists a residue class \(r\bmod D_A\) and a constant
-    \(c>0\) such that
-    \[
-      \frac{a_{r+kD_A}(\mathcal A)}{b^{r+kD_A}}\ge c
-      \qquad\text{for all sufficiently large }k.
-    \]
-  \end{enumerate}
-  In particular, no DFA language can satisfy
-  \[
-    a_m(\mathcal A)/b^m\asymp m^{-\alpha}
-  \]
-  for any \(\alpha>0\). More generally, there do not exist
-  \(K_1,K_2>0\) and an infinite set \(M\subseteq\NN\) such that
-  \[
-    \frac{K_1}{m}\le \frac{a_m(\mathcal A)}{b^m}\le \frac{K_2}{m}
-    \qquad(m\in M).
-  \]
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-  For each digit \(d\in\Sigma_b\), let \(T_d\in\{0,1\}^{Q\times Q}\) be
-  the transition matrix for \(d\), and let
-  \[
-    B:=\sum_{d\in\Sigma_b}T_d.
-  \]
-  Since the automaton is complete and deterministic, every row sum of
-  \(B\) is equal to \(b\). If \(u\) is the indicator vector of the
-  initial state and \(v\) is the indicator of the accepting set, then
-  \[
-    a_m(\mathcal A)=u^{\mathsf T}B^m v.
-  \]
-  Set \(P:=B/b\). Then \(P\) is a stochastic matrix on the finite set
-  \(Q\). After permuting states, put \(P\) in canonical Markov-chain
-  form
-  \[
-    P=
-    \begin{pmatrix}
-      T & R_1 & \cdots & R_s\\
-      0 & C_1 & 0 & 0\\
-      \vdots & 0 & \ddots & 0\\
-      0 & 0 & 0 & C_s
-    \end{pmatrix},
-  \]
-  where \(T\) is the transient block, \(\rho(T)<1\), and each \(C_i\)
-  is an irreducible stochastic recurrent class. For \(m\ge1\),
-  \[
-    P^m=
-    \begin{pmatrix}
-      T^m &
-      \sum_{\ell=0}^{m-1}T^\ell R_1C_1^{m-1-\ell} &
-      \cdots &
-      \sum_{\ell=0}^{m-1}T^\ell R_sC_s^{m-1-\ell}\\
-      0 & C_1^m & 0 & 0\\
-      \vdots & 0 & \ddots & 0\\
-      0 & 0 & 0 & C_s^m
-    \end{pmatrix}.
-  \]
-  Thus the transient-to-recurrent blocks need not be exponentially
-  small: their absorption convolutions generally converge to non-zero
-  periodic limits.
-
-  Let \(d_i\) be the period of \(C_i\), and put
-  \(D_A:=\operatorname{lcm}(d_1,\dots,d_s)\). By the periodic
-  Perron--Frobenius theorem for the recurrent blocks, each sequence
-  \(C_i^{kD_A+r}\) converges exponentially fast as \(k\to\infty\), for
-  each fixed \(r\). Since \(T^\ell\) decays exponentially, the displayed
-  convolution also has an exponentially fast limit on every residue
-  class. Hence the entrywise limits
-  \[
-    S_r:=\lim_{k\to\infty}P^{kD_A+r}
-    \qquad(0\le r<D_A)
-  \]
-  exist; the matrices \(S_r\) include both the recurrent-class limits
-  and the absorption terms from transient states into those recurrent
-  classes. This theorem uses these as qualitative Markov-chain limits;
-  the certified computable version, with rational tail constants and
-  verifiable proof objects, is isolated in
-  \Cref{lem:effective-spectral-constants,thm:effective-fixed-dfa-prime-obstruction}.
-  Consequently there are \(C>0\) and \(\theta\in(0,1)\) such
-  that
-  \[
-    P^m=S_{m\bmod D_A}+E_m,
-    \qquad
-    \|E_m\|\le C\theta^m.
-  \]
-  Therefore
-  \[
-    u^{\mathsf T}P^m v=u^{\mathsf T}S_{m\bmod D_A}v+O(\theta^m).
-  \]
-  For \(0\le r<D_A\), define
-  \[
-    c_r:=\lim_{k\to\infty}u^{\mathsf T}P^{kD_A+r}v=u^{\mathsf T}S_r v.
-  \]
-  The limit exists by the preceding expansion, and \(c_r\ge 0\) because
-  every term \(u^{\mathsf T}P^{kD_A+r}v\) is non-negative. Thus
-  \[
-    \frac{a_m(\mathcal A)}{b^m}
-    =u^{\mathsf T}P^m v
-    =c_{m\bmod D_A}+O(\theta^m),
-  \]
-  as claimed.
-
-  If every \(c_r\) vanishes, then
-  \(a_m(\mathcal A)/b^m=O(\theta^m)\), which is alternative
-  \textup{(i)}. Otherwise some \(c_r\) is strictly positive, and along
-  the corresponding residue class the density has a positive lower
-  bound, which is alternative \textup{(ii)}.
-
-  The exclusion of intermediate polynomial density follows by the same
-  residue-class argument. Suppose first that
-  \(a_m(\mathcal A)/b^m\asymp m^{-\alpha}\) for some \(\alpha>0\).
-  If all \(c_r\) vanish, then \(a_m(\mathcal A)/b^m=O(\theta^m)\), which
-  is eventually smaller than every positive multiple of \(m^{-\alpha}\).
-  If some \(c_r>0\), then along that residue class
-  \(a_m(\mathcal A)/b^m\ge c_r/2\) for all sufficiently large \(m\),
-  which is incompatible with an upper bound \(O(m^{-\alpha})\).
-  Finally, suppose that for some \(K_1,K_2>0\) the two-sided
-  finite-budget bound \(K_1/m\le a_m(\mathcal A)/b^m\le K_2/m\) holds
-  on an infinite set \(M\). Passing to an infinite subset in one residue
-  class \(r\bmod D_A\), the case \(c_r=0\) contradicts the lower bound
-  \(K_1/m\), while the case \(c_r>0\) contradicts the upper bound
-  \(K_2/m\). This proves the final assertion.
-\end{proof}
-
-For later use we spell out the elementary effective content of the
-preceding proof. Assume that the entries of the DFA transition matrices
-are given explicitly. Put \(P=B/b\). The strongly connected components
-of the directed graph of \(P\), the recurrent classes, their periods
-\(d_i\), and hence \(D_A=\operatorname{lcm}(d_i)\), are obtained by the
-standard linear-time graph algorithms. For each residue class \(r\bmod
-D_A\), the limit
-\[
-  c_r=\lim_{k\to\infty}u^{\mathsf T}P^{kD_A+r}v
-\]
-is the value of the finite Markov chain on that residue class; it can be
-computed by solving the finite linear systems for the stationary
-distributions on the recurrent classes and the absorption probabilities
-from transient states. Equivalently, it is obtained as the exact
-limit of the rational matrices \(P^{kD_A+r}\). Thus the residue
-alternatives \(c_r=0\) and \(c_r>0\) are decidable by exact rational
-linear algebra when the transition table is integral.
-
-This density dichotomy is classical; compare
-\cite{Berstel1973,BodirskyGaertnerVonOertzenSchwinghammer2004,Bell2020UpperDensity,Koga2019Density}.
-It is not the new ingredient of the paper; we keep the short proof
-because the residue-class constants are the input certified in
-\Cref{thm:effective-fixed-dfa-prime-obstruction} and then used in the
-prime corollaries below.
-
-\begin{lemma}[Explicit prime-counting input]
-  \label{lem:explicit-pnt-input}
-  The following numerical constants are admissible:
-  \[
-    X_0=355991,\qquad C_{\pi,1}=2,\qquad C_{\pi,2}=2.
-  \]
-  For every \(x\ge X_0\),
-  \[
-    \left|\pi(x)-\frac{x}{\log x}\right|
-      \le C_{\pi,1}\frac{x}{(\log x)^2},
-    \qquad
-    \pi(x)\le C_{\pi,2}\frac{x}{\log x}.
-  \]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-  Rosser--Schoenfeld prove \(\pi(x)>x/\log x\) for \(x\ge17\)
-  \cite{RosserSchoenfeld1962}. Dusart's published explicit upper
-  estimate \cite[Theorem~1.10]{Dusart2018} gives
-  \[
-    \pi(x)\le
-      \frac{x}{\log x}\left(1+\frac{1}{\log x}
-        +\frac{2.51}{(\log x)^2}\right)
-    \qquad (x\ge355991).
-  \]
-  These are the exact published inputs used here. Since
-  \(\log 355991>12\), for \(x\ge355991\) we have
-  \[
-    0\le \pi(x)-\frac{x}{\log x}
-    \le \frac{x}{(\log x)^2}
-       +2.51\,\frac{x}{(\log x)^3}
-    \le 2\,\frac{x}{(\log x)^2},
-  \]
-  and also
-  \[
-    \pi(x)\le
-      \frac{x}{\log x}\left(1+\frac{1}{\log x}
-        +\frac{2.51}{(\log x)^2}\right)
-      \le 2\,\frac{x}{\log x}.
-  \]
-\end{proof}
-
-We shall use the following interval-count convention in both prime-slice
-estimates. For \(X<Y\) with \(X\ge X_0\),
-\[
-  \#\{p\text{ prime}:X\le p<Y\}
-  =\pi(Y)-\pi(X)+\varepsilon_{X,Y},
-  \qquad |\varepsilon_{X,Y}|\le2.
-\]
-Thus all half-open endpoint changes in the slice estimates are accounted
-for by one absolute \(O(1)\) term.
-
-\begin{remark}\label{rem:dfa-density-sharpness}
-  Both alternatives occur already for elementary regular languages. The
-  language \(\Sigma_b^\ast 0\) of words ending in \(0\) has density
-  \(1/b\) in every positive length, so it lies in
-  alternative~\textup{(ii)}. By contrast, the language \(0^\ast 1\)
-  satisfies \(\#(0^\ast 1\cap\Sigma_b^m)=1\) for every \(m\ge 1\), so
-  its normalized density is \(b^{-m}\). It therefore lies in the
-  normalized exponential-sparse alternative~\textup{(i)} even though
-  the raw count is constant rather than decreasing.
-\end{remark}
-
-For base-\(b\) expansions we use the standard most-significant-digit
-first convention: a word \(d_1\cdots d_m\in\Sigma_b^m\) represents the
-integer \(\sum_{j=1}^m d_j b^{m-j}\). For each \(m\ge 1\), let
-\(\mathcal P_m^{(b)}\) be the set of base-\(b\) words of length \(m\)
-whose first digit is nonzero and whose value is prime. Let
-\(p_m^{(b)}:=\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}\). By the prime number theorem
-\cite{HardyWright2008},
-\[
-  p_m^{(b)}
-  =\pi(b^m-1)-\pi(b^{m-1}-1)
-  \asymp \frac{b^m}{m}.
-\]
-The condition that the first digit be nonzero excludes leading zeros.
-One may equivalently compare a DFA language against
-\(\{1,\dots,b-1\}\Sigma_b^{m-1}\); in particular, the scale
-\(\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}\asymp b^m/m\) is unchanged because every
-prime in \([b^{m-1},b^m)\) already has base-\(b\) length \(m\).
-
-\begin{lemma}[Prime counts in base-\(b\) slices]
-  \label{lem:base-prime-count}
-  Let \(X_0,C_{\pi,1},C_{\pi,2}\) be constants satisfying
-  \Cref{lem:explicit-pnt-input}. There are explicit constants
-  \(A_b,B_b>0\) and an explicit integer \(M_b\) such that, for all
-  \(m\ge M_b\),
-  \[
-    A_b\,\frac{b^m}{m}
-    \le \abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}
-    \le B_b\,\frac{b^m}{m}.
-  \]
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-  Put \(L_b:=\log b\). The threshold used below is obtained by the
-  following finite algorithm. Start with
-  \(M\ge2\) satisfying \(b^{M-1}\ge X_0\). Increase \(M\) until
-  \(1-m/(b(m-1))\ge(1-1/b)/2\) for all \(m\ge M\), which is certified
-  from the identity
-  \(1-m/(b(m-1))=(b-1)/b-1/(b(m-1))\). Then increase \(M\) until
-  \[
-    C_{\pi,1}\left(\frac{1}{mL_b^2}
-      +\frac{m}{b(m-1)^2L_b^2}\right)
-      +\frac{2m}{b^m}
-    \le
-    \frac{1}{2L_b}
-      \left(1-\frac{m}{b(m-1)}\right).
-  \]
-  To make the last step reproducible, note that the two rational
-  functions \(1/m\) and \(m/(m-1)^2\) are decreasing for \(m\ge2\), and
-  \(m/b^m\) is decreasing for \(m\ge1/\log b\). The right-hand side is
-  increasing in \(m\). Thus after
-  \(M_{\mathrm{mon}}:=\max\{2,\lceil1/\log b\rceil+1\}\), it is enough
-  to test the displayed inequality at the candidate value \(M\); the
-  finitely many smaller \(m\) between the initial lower bound and
-  \(M_{\mathrm{mon}}\) are checked directly. Let \(M_b\) be the first
-  candidate accepted by this procedure. This produces a reproducible
-  value of \(M_b\), not an unspecified asymptotic threshold.
-  The leading-digit convention gives the exact half-open interval count
-  \[
-    \abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}=\pi(b^m-1)-\pi(b^{m-1}-1).
-  \]
-  Applying the interval-count convention after
-  \Cref{lem:explicit-pnt-input}, the endpoint correction is the visible
-  inequality
-  \[
-    \left|
-      \abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}-
-      \bigl(\pi(b^m)-\pi(b^{m-1})\bigr)
-    \right|\le 2,
-  \]
-  valid for every \(m\ge1\). Equivalently, this is
-  \[
-    \pi(b^m)-\pi(b^{m-1})+O(1),
-  \]
-  with the displayed absolute constant. For \(m\ge M_b\), the explicit
-  estimate in \Cref{lem:explicit-pnt-input} gives
-  \[
-    \begin{aligned}
-    \pi(b^m)-\pi(b^{m-1})
-    \ge
-    &\frac{b^m}{m\log b}
-      -\frac{b^{m-1}}{(m-1)\log b}\\
-    &{}-C_{\pi,1}\frac{b^m}{m^2(\log b)^2}
-      -C_{\pi,1}\frac{b^{m-1}}{(m-1)^2(\log b)^2}.
-    \end{aligned}
-  \]
-  Since
-  \[
-    \frac{b^m}{m\log b}
-    -\frac{b^{m-1}}{(m-1)\log b}
-    =
-    \frac{b^m}{m\log b}
-    \left(1-\frac{m}{b(m-1)}\right),
-  \]
-  the choice of \(M_b\), together with the endpoint \(O(1)\), gives the
-  explicit lower bound
-  \[
-    \abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}
-    \ge
-    \frac{1}{2\log b}
-    \left(1-\frac{m}{b(m-1)}\right)\frac{b^m}{m}.
-  \]
-  By construction,
-  \(1-m/(b(m-1))\ge (1-1/b)/2\), so one may take
-  \[
-    A_b:=\frac{1-1/b}{4\log b}.
-  \]
-  The upper bound follows from
-  \[
-    \abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}\le\pi(b^m)
-      \le C_{\pi,2}\frac{b^m}{m\log b},
-  \]
-  so \(B_b:=C_{\pi,2}/\log b\) is admissible for all \(m\ge M_b\).
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Certified spectral decay for a fixed residue class]
-  \label{lem:effective-spectral-constants}
-  Let \(P\) be a rational stochastic matrix. Suppose that the recurrent
-  classes and their cyclic decompositions have been computed, and let
-  \(D_A\) be a common multiple of the recurrent periods. For each
-  residue class \(r\bmod D_A\) there is an algorithm which outputs
-  rational numbers \(0<\tau_r<\theta_r<1\), \(K_r>0\), and an integer
-  \(N_r\) such that
-  \[
-    \|P^m-S_r\|_\infty\le K_r\theta_r^m
-    \qquad(m\equiv r\bmod D_A,\ m\ge N_r),
-  \]
-  where \(S_r=\lim_{k\to\infty}P^{kD_A+r}\). The output includes a
-  finite certificate consisting of the strict inequalities
-  \[
-    \rho(T)<\tau_r,\qquad
-    \rho(Q_{j,t}-\Pi_{j,t})<\tau_r^{d_j},
-  \]
-  where \(T=P_{TT}\), \(Q_{j,t}=P^{d_j}|_{R_{j,t}}\) is the primitive
-  return chain on the cyclic class \(R_{j,t}\), and
-  \(\Pi_{j,t}=\mathbf 1\pi_{j,t}\), plus rational resolvent bounds. The
-  proof object also records, for each residue, an integer polynomial
-  degree \(J_r\), a monotonicity threshold for the inequality
-  \(C_rm^{J_r}\tau_r^m\le K_r\theta_r^m\), and the finite list of exact
-  rational matrix inequalities checked below that threshold. We assert
-  computability of these data; no polynomial bit-complexity or
-  output-sensitive complexity bound is claimed.
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-  Put \(P\) in canonical Markov-chain block form. The decaying blocks
-  are the transient block \(T=P_{TT}\) and, for each recurrent cyclic
-  class \(R_{j,t}\), the return-error block
-  \(E_{j,t}:=Q_{j,t}-\Pi_{j,t}\). The block \(T\) has spectral radius
-  \(<1\), and each \(E_{j,t}\) has spectral radius \(<1\) because
-  \(Q_{j,t}\) is primitive stochastic.
-
-  Compute the characteristic polynomials of these rational blocks and
-  isolate their complex roots as algebraic numbers. If the finite list
-  of roots is empty, take \(\tau_r=1/3\) and \(\theta_r=1/2\). Otherwise
-  choose a rational \(\tau_r\in(0,1)\) such that all eigenvalues of
-  \(T\) have modulus \(<\tau_r\) and all eigenvalues of every
-  \(E_{j,t}\) have modulus \(<\tau_r^{d_j}\); then choose any rational
-  \(\theta_r\) with \(\tau_r<\theta_r<1\). Each strict comparison is
-  certified by rational isolating rectangles whose squared moduli lie
-  below the corresponding rational threshold. This gives the
-  spectral-radius part of the certificate, including the case in which
-  there are no non-peripheral roots to control.
-
-  It remains to turn spectral separation into a bound on powers without
-  invoking a Jordan basis. Let \(A\) be any one of the rational blocks
-  and let \(\eta\in(0,1)\) be the corresponding block rate
-  (\(\eta=\tau_r\) for \(T\), and
-  \(\eta=\tau_r^{d_j}\) for \(E_{j,t}\)). Choose a rational
-  \(\gamma\) with \(\rho(A)<\gamma<\eta\). From the root isolating
-  rectangles we compute a rational \(\delta>0\) such that
-  \[
-    |\det(zI-A)|\ge\delta\qquad(|z|=\gamma).
-  \]
-  Indeed, if \(R_\xi\) is the isolating rectangle for a root \(\xi\),
-  exact rational interval arithmetic gives a positive rational lower
-  bound \(\Delta_\xi\) for
-  \(\inf\{|z-w|:|z|=\gamma,\ w\in R_\xi\}\); positivity follows from
-  \(\rho(A)<\gamma\) and from the disjoint certified rectangles. The
-  characteristic polynomial is monic, so the
-  product \(\prod_\xi\Delta_\xi\) is a valid determinant lower bound,
-  with one factor for each root counted with algebraic multiplicity. The
-  adjugate entries of
-  \(zI-A\) are polynomials in \(z\), so their absolute values on the
-  same circle have an elementary rational upper bound \(U\) obtained
-  from the coefficients of \(A\) and the identity \(|z|=\gamma\).
-  Cauchy's formula
-  for the matrix resolvent gives
-  \[
-    A^m=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{|z|=\gamma}z^m(zI-A)^{-1}\,dz,
-    \qquad
-    \|A^m\|_\infty\le L_A\gamma^m\le L_A\eta^m,
-  \]
-  where \(L_A\) is a rational number computed from \(U,\delta,\gamma\),
-  and the dimension of \(A\). The data
-  \((\gamma,\delta,U,L_A)\) are the resolvent certificate for \(A\).
-
-  We now spell out the finite block normal form used by the verifier.
-  In the canonical order \(T,R_1,\ldots,R_s\), and for
-  \(m\equiv r\bmod D_A\), the only non-zero blocks of \(P^m-S_r\) are
-  of the following types.
-  \[
-    T^m,\qquad C_j^m-C_{j,r}^{\infty},
-  \]
-  on the diagonal, and
-  \[
-    \sum_{\ell=0}^{m-1}
-      T^\ell P_{T,R_j}\bigl(C_j^{m-1-\ell}-C_{j,r-\ell-1}^{\infty}\bigr)
-      -
-    \sum_{\ell=m}^{\infty}
-      T^\ell P_{T,R_j}C_{j,r-\ell-1}^{\infty}
-  \]
-  in the transient-to-\(R_j\) block. Here \(C_{j,a}^{\infty}\) is the
-  rational limit of \(C_j^n\) along \(n\equiv a\bmod d_j\); explicitly
-  its rows supported on \(R_{j,t}\) are equal to
-  \(\pi_{j,t+a}\) on \(R_{j,t+a}\) and zero elsewhere. For each
-  \(a\bmod d_j\) let
-  \(G_{j,u}:=P_{R_{j,u},R_{j,u+1}}\) and
-  \(W_{j,t,a}:=G_{j,t}G_{j,t+1}\cdots G_{j,t+a-1}\), with
-  \(W_{j,t,0}\) the identity on \(R_{j,t}\). The certificate expands
-  \(C_j^{d_jh+a}-C_{j,a}^{\infty}\), for \(h\ge1\), as the finite
-  rational sum
-  \[
-    \sum_{t=0}^{d_j-1}
-      M_{j,t,a}(h),
-  \]
-  where \(M_{j,t,a}(h)\) is the full \(R_j\times R_j\) matrix whose only
-  non-zero block is the block from rows \(R_{j,t}\) to columns
-  \(R_{j,t+a}\), equal to \(W_{j,t,a}E_{j,t+a}^{h}\). The case \(h=0\)
-  is one of the finitely many initial powers checked directly. The
-  verifier checks the identity for \(0\le a<d_j\) by multiplying the
-  listed rational cyclic blocks and using
-  \(Q_{j,t+a}^{h}-\Pi_{j,t+a}=E_{j,t+a}^{h}\) for \(h\ge1\). Thus every
-  summand is a listed rational connector product containing either
-  \(T^n\), one \(E_{j,t}^n\), or one convolution of such powers.
-
-  The resolvent bounds above dominate a listed direct product
-  \(X A^n Y\) by
-  \(\|X\|_\infty L_A\|Y\|_\infty\eta^n\). A listed finite convolution is
-  first split by writing \(\ell=u+D_Aq\). If
-  \(m-1-u=d_jH_{m,u}+a\), with \(0\le a<d_j\), then its recurrent
-  return-error exponent is \(H_{m,u}-L_jq\), where
-  \(L_j=D_A/d_j\). Thus a residue summand has the form
-  \[
-    \sum_q X_uT^{D_Aq}Y_uE_{j,t_u}^{H_{m,u}-L_jq}Z_u,
-  \]
-  with the terms having non-positive recurrent exponent placed in the
-  finite direct-check list. For the remaining terms the product of the
-  two exponential bounds, with the finite \(T^u\) factor already included
-  in the rational connector \(X_u\), is
-  \[
-    \tau_r^{D_Aq}\tau_r^{d_jH_{m,u}-D_Aq}
-      =\tau_r^{m-1-u-a},
-  \]
-  so the \(q\)-dependence cancels. Since there are at most \(m\) terms
-  and only finitely many residues \(u,a\), exact rational norm bounds
-  give a listed inequality \(C\,m\tau_r^m\) after absorbing
-  \(\tau_r^{-1-u-a}\) into \(C\). The infinite tail above is bounded by the
-  listed geometric estimate
-  \[
-    \sum_{\ell=m}^{\infty}
-      \|T^\ell\|_\infty\|P_{T,R_j}\|_\infty
-      \|C_{j,r-\ell-1}^{\infty}\|_\infty
-    \le
-    \frac{L_T\|P_{T,R_j}\|_\infty}{1-\tau_r}\tau_r^m .
-  \]
-  Adding the finitely many rational coefficients gives explicit
-  \(C_r>0\) and \(J_r\le1\) with
-  \[
-    \|P^m-S_r\|_\infty\le C_rm^{J_r}\tau_r^m
-    \qquad(m\equiv r\bmod D_A),
-  \]
-  after increasing \(C_r\) to absorb the finitely many omitted small
-  exponents and the finite factors
-  \(\max_{0\le u<D_A,\ 0\le a<d_j}\tau_r^{-1-u-a}\). This is the only
-  polynomial loss retained in the certificate: the block and convolution
-  estimates are first made at the strict rate \(\tau_r\), and the final
-  advertised rate \(\theta_r\) is introduced only after choosing
-  \(\theta_r\in(\tau_r,1)\). Since \(\tau_r/\theta_r<1\), the rational
-  sequence \(m^{J_r}(\tau_r/\theta_r)^m\) is eventually decreasing and
-  tends to \(0\). A finite rational search therefore produces \(K_r\)
-  and \(N_r\) such that
-  \[
-    C_rm^{J_r}\tau_r^m\le K_r\theta_r^m
-    \qquad(m\ge N_r).
-  \]
-  The certificate records both rates, namely the block rate \(\tau_r\)
-  and the final output rate \(\theta_r\), together with
-  \(C_r,J_r,K_r,N_r\) and the explicit monotone-tail threshold. The
-  finitely many powers in the
-  residue class below that threshold are checked directly by rational
-  matrix powering and are included as exact inequalities; if necessary,
-  \(K_r\) is enlarged before the certificate is printed. Thus the
-  certificate verifies the displayed inequality for all
-  \(m\equiv r\bmod D_A\) with \(m\ge N_r\).
-
-  Thus the verifier never appeals to an unnamed finite-chain formula.
-  Its normal form for each entry of \(P^m-S_r\) is the explicit finite
-  list consisting of the direct transient powers \(T^m\), the recurrent
-  return-error terms \(W_{j,t,a}E_{j,t+a}^h\), the residue-grouped
-  convolutions just displayed, and the geometric resolvent tails
-  \((I-T^{D_A})^{-1}T^u\). Each listed matrix is rational once the
-  stationary vectors and cyclic projections have been solved over
-  \(\QQ\), and each inequality is reduced to rational norm bounds plus
-  the certified root-isolation comparisons above.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{theorem}[Algorithmic fixed-DFA prime-slice obstruction]
-  \label{thm:effective-fixed-dfa-prime-obstruction}
-  Fix \(b\ge2\) and a complete DFA
-  \(\mathcal A=(Q,\Sigma_b,\delta,q_0,F)\), encoded by its integer
-  transition table. Let \(B\) be its unlabeled transition matrix and
-  \(P=B/b\). There is an algorithm which outputs the following
-  compressed exact certificate.
-  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
-    \item The transient set \(T\), the recurrent classes
-    \(R_1,\dots,R_s\) of \(P\), their periods \(d_j\), and cyclic
-    decompositions \(R_{j,0},\dots,R_{j,d_j-1}\).
-    \item For every \(j,t\), the stationary probability vector
-    \(\pi_{j,t}\) of the primitive return chain
-    \(P^{d_j}|_{R_{j,t}}\), with rational entries.
-    \item The absorption probabilities \(H_j(q)\), \(q\in T\), obtained
-    from
-    \[
-      (I-P_{TT})H_j=P_{T,R_j}\mathbf 1,
-    \]
-    and the refined cyclic absorption probabilities
-    \[
-      A_{j,t}(q)
-      :=\sum_{\ell\ge0}
-        e_q^{\mathsf T}P_{TT}^{\ell}P_{T,R_j}
-        S_{j,t+\ell+1}\mathbf 1 ,
-    \]
-    where indices are taken modulo \(d_j\) and
-    \(S_{j,u}\) is the cyclic projection onto \(R_{j,u}\).
-    Thus, conditional on absorption after \(\ell\) transient steps, the
-    recurrent entry class is chosen so that at every later time
-    \(m\equiv r\pmod {d_j}\) the recurrent chain lies in
-    \(R_{j,t+r}\). The displayed series is evaluated exactly as a
-    finite family of linear solves after grouping \(\ell\) modulo
-    \(d_j\), namely
-    \[
-      A_{j,t}
-      =
-      \sum_{u=0}^{d_j-1}
-      (I-P_{TT}^{d_j})^{-1}P_{TT}^uP_{T,R_j}
-      S_{j,t+u+1}\mathbf 1 .
-    \]
-    \item For each residue \(r\) modulo
-    \(D_A=\operatorname{lcm}_j d_j\), the compressed formula
-    \[
-      c_r=
-      \sum_{j=1}^s\sum_{t=0}^{d_j-1}

-    numbers \(\tau_r,\theta_r\), rational upper bounds \(K_r\), the
-    monotone tail threshold, and the finite list of exact rational
-    inequalities checked before the tail. These data are enough to
-    verify the inequality mechanically, without reconstructing an
-    algebraic Jordan basis.

-  \smallskip
-  \noindent\textit{Certificate schema.}
-  For each residue class the certificate schema consists of the
-  following fields, all represented by rational data except for the
-  root-isolation rectangles.
-  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
-    \item Rational matrices \(P,T,Q_{j,t},E_{j,t}=Q_{j,t}-\Pi_{j,t}\),

-    \(\pi_{j,t},A_{j,t}\) solving the displayed linear systems.

-    \item Rational numbers \(c_r,\tau_r,\theta_r,K_r,C_r\), integers
-    \(J_r,N_r\), and a tail threshold \(N_r^{\mathrm{tail}}\), with

-    root and disjoint from the others, whose squared-modulus intervals
-    certify \(\rho(T)<\tau_r\) and
-    \(\rho(E_{j,t})<\tau_r^{d_j}\). The verifier checks these by
-    Sturm--subdivision or any equivalent exact rational root-counting
-    procedure on the rectangles and by rational interval arithmetic for
-    the squared moduli.
-    \item Resolvent certificates
-    \((\gamma_A,\delta_A,U_A,L_A)\) for
-    \(A\in\{T\}\cup\{E_{j,t}\}_{j,t}\), with
-    \(\rho(A)<\gamma_A<\tau_r\) for \(A=T\) and
-    \(\rho(A)<\gamma_A<\tau_r^{d_j}\) for \(A=E_{j,t}\). The verifier
-    checks, using the same isolating rectangles and rational interval
-    arithmetic, that every rectangle lies strictly inside the circle
-    \(|z|=\gamma_A\) and supplies a positive rational distance
-    \(\Delta_\xi\) from the rectangle to that circle. Therefore
-    \[
-      |\det(zI-A)|\ge \prod_{\xi}\Delta_\xi=:\delta_A
-      \qquad(|z|=\gamma_A),
-    \]
-    with roots counted with algebraic multiplicity. The verifier also
-    checks the elementary coefficient bound
-    \[
-      \|\operatorname{adj}(zI-A)\|_\infty\le U_A,
-    \]

-    class \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_A}\). For every recurrent block \(R_j\)

-    the data also include the exact identity
-    \[
-      (P^m-S_r)_{T,R_j}
-      =
-      \sum_{\ell=0}^{m-1}

-      h=H_{m,u}-L_jq,\qquad
-      L_j:=D_A/d_j,\qquad
-      H_{m,u}:=(m-1-u-a)/d_j .
-    \]

-    \[

-  \noindent\textit{Certificate-verifier theorem.}
-  Given the fields just listed, there is a finite verifier which accepts
-  if and only if the following rational assertions all check:
-  the stochastic block decomposition is a permutation of \(P\); each
-  \(C_{j,a}^{\infty}\), \(\pi_{j,t}\), and \(A_{j,t}\) satisfies its
-  displayed linear equations; the root-isolation rectangles prove the
-  strict spectral-radius inequalities; the resolvent certificates prove
-  the listed bounds for every decaying block; the finite block normal
-  form for \(P^m-S_r\) is exactly the one displayed in the preceding
-  two items; the summed direct, convolution, and tail coefficients give
-  \(\|P^m-S_r\|_\infty\le C_rm^{J_r}\tau_r^m\) on the residue class;
-  the finitely many pre-tail powers satisfy the same advertised
-  estimate after enlargement of \(K_r\); and the rational monotone-tail
-  inequality gives \(C_rm^{J_r}\tau_r^m\le K_r\theta_r^m\). All steps
-  use rational matrix arithmetic, exact inverses over \(\QQ\), finite
-  root counts in rational rectangles, and rational interval arithmetic.
-  No unlisted block formula or limiting argument is part of the
-  verification step.
-  With this output, the following holds for every
-  \(m\ge M_r\) satisfying \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_A}\).
-  If \(c_r=0\), then
-  \[
-    a_m(\mathcal A)\le K_r\theta_r^m b^m
-    \quad\text{and}\quad
-    \abs{(L(\mathcal A)\cap\Sigma_b^m)\triangle\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}
-    \ge \frac{A_b}{2}\,\frac{b^m}{m}.
-  \]
-  If \(c_r>0\), then
-  \[
-    a_m(\mathcal A)\ge \frac{c_r}{2}b^m,
-    \qquad
-    \mathrm{Prec}_m\le \frac{2B_b}{c_r}\,\frac1m,
-  \]
-  whenever \(\mathrm{Prec}_m\) is defined, i.e. on lengths where the
-  denominator is nonzero, and
-  \[
-    \abs{(L(\mathcal A)\cap\Sigma_b^m)\triangle\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}
-    \ge \frac{c_r}{4} b^m .
-  \]
-  Here \(A_b,B_b,M_b\) may be the explicit constants supplied by
-  \Cref{lem:base-prime-count}. Consequently
-  one computes constants \(c_{\mathcal A,b}>0\) and \(M_{\mathcal A,b}\)
-  such that
-  \[
-    \abs{(L(\mathcal A)\cap\Sigma_b^m)\triangle\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}
-    \ge c_{\mathcal A,b}\,\frac{b^m}{m}
-    \qquad(m\ge M_{\mathcal A,b}).
-  \]
-  The compressed output is the tuple
-  \[
-    \mathcal C=(D_A,\{R_j,d_j,(R_{j,t})_t,\pi_{j,t},A_{j,t}\}_{j,t},
-      \{c_r,\tau_r,\theta_r,K_r,C_r,J_r,N_r,M_r\}_{r\bmod D_A})
-  \]
-  when all residues are enumerated. If \(D_A\) is large, the same data
-  may instead be represented by the class list together with an exact
-  residue-evaluation procedure for
-  \(r\mapsto c_r,\tau_r,\theta_r,K_r,C_r,J_r,N_r,M_r\) and the
-  corresponding proof object from part~\textup{(e)};
-  any final all-large constant obtained by taking a minimum over
-  residues is then represented by this finite minimization procedure.
-  Printing the full residue table is charged to output size \(D_A\).
-  No polynomial bound in the input size alone is asserted for the
-  spectral certificate, for enumerating all residues, or for the final
-  minimization.
-\end{theorem}

-\begin{proof}
-  Compute the matrix \(B=\sum_{d\in\Sigma_b}T_d\), the stochastic matrix
-  \(P=B/b\), the transient set, the recurrent classes, their periods,
-  their cyclic decompositions, and the common period \(D_A\) by standard
-  graph algorithms. The vectors \(\pi_{j,t}\) are the unique solutions
-  of
-  \[
-    \pi_{j,t}P^{d_j}|_{R_{j,t}}=\pi_{j,t},
-    \qquad
-    \pi_{j,t}\mathbf 1=1.
-  \]
-  Because \(P\) has rational entries, these vectors are rational and
-  are obtained by rational Gaussian elimination. The absorption
-  probabilities \(H_j\) solve the displayed systems in the statement;
-  the matrix \(I-P_{TT}\) is invertible because \(T\) is transient.
-  For the cyclic refinements, group the defining series for
-  \(A_{j,t}\) by \(\ell\equiv u\pmod{d_j}\). Each group is a
-  rational expression in
-  \[
-    (I-P_{TT}^{d_j})^{-1}P_{TT}^uP_{T,R_j}S_{j,t+u+1}\mathbf 1,
-  \]
-  hence is again computed by exact rational linear algebra. Formula
-  \eqref{eq:compressed-cr} is precisely the canonical block-power limit
-  of \(u^{\mathsf T}P^m v\) along \(m\equiv r\pmod {D_A}\). Indeed,
-  suppose the chain starts in a transient state \(q\), remains
-  transient for exactly \(\ell\) steps, and then enters \(R_j\) at time
-  \(\ell+1\) in cyclic class \(R_{j,u}\). Because \(P\) maps
-  \(R_{j,a}\) into \(R_{j,a+1}\), at a later time
-  \(m\equiv r\pmod {d_j}\) its recurrent cyclic class is
-  \[
-    u+m-(\ell+1)\equiv u+r-\ell-1 \pmod {d_j}.
-  \]
-  To contribute to the limiting distribution
-  \(\pi_{j,t+r}\) on \(R_{j,t+r}\), the entry class must therefore
-  satisfy \(u+r-\ell-1\equiv t+r\), equivalently
-  \(u\equiv t+\ell+1\pmod {d_j}\). This is exactly the projection
-  \(S_{j,t+\ell+1}\) in the definition of \(A_{j,t}\). Conditioning on
-  the absorption time and then applying the primitive return-chain limit
-  on \(R_{j,t+r}\) proves \eqref{eq:compressed-cr}.
-
-  Applying \Cref{lem:effective-spectral-constants} to \(P\) and
-  \(D_A\) gives \(\tau_r,\theta_r,K_r,N_r\) and
-  \[
-    \abs{a_m(\mathcal A)/b^m-c_r}\le K_r\theta_r^m
-    \qquad(m\equiv r\bmod {D_A},\ m\ge N_r).
-  \]
-  The associated certificate consists of rational
-  \(\tau_r,\theta_r,K_r,C_r\), the integer \(J_r\), the
-  spectral-radius proof objects for the transient and return-error
-  blocks, the rational resolvent bounds, the rational inequality
-  \(C_rm^{J_r}\tau_r^m\le K_r\theta_r^m\) on the tail, and the finite
-  rational power checks preceding the tail. Thus the quantified
-  inequality used below is part of the output, not an unverifiable
-  analytic side condition.
-
-  Choose \(A_b,B_b>0\) and \(M_b\) from
-  \Cref{lem:base-prime-count}, so that
-  \[
-    A_b\,\frac{b^m}{m}
-    \le\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}
-    \le B_b\,\frac{b^m}{m}
-    \qquad(m\ge M_b).
-  \]
-  If \(c_r=0\), take \(M_r\ge \max(M_b,N_r)\) to be any integer in the
-  residue class tail satisfying
-  \[
-    K_r\theta_r^m\le \frac{A_b}{2m}
-    \qquad(m\ge M_r,\ m\equiv r\bmod {D_A}).
-  \]
-  Since \(K_r\) and \(\theta_r\) are rational, this threshold is
-  obtained by checking finitely many values before monotonicity of
-  \(mK_r\theta_r^m\) begins and then recording the first value after
-  which the monotone tail is below \(A_b/2\).
-  For \(m\ge M_r\) with \(m\equiv r\bmod {D_A}\),
-  \[
-    a_m(\mathcal A)\le \frac{A_b}{2}\frac{b^m}{m},
-  \]
-  so the symmetric difference is at least
-  \(A_b b^m/(2m)\).
-
-  If \(c_r>0\), take \(M_r\ge \max(M_b,N_r)\) so that
-  \[
-    K_r\theta_r^m\le c_r/2,
-    \qquad
-    B_b/m\le c_r/4
-  \]
-  for all \(m\ge M_r\) with \(m\equiv r\bmod {D_A}\). This is again a
-  rational monotone-tail check.
-  Then \(a_m(\mathcal A)\ge(c_r/2)b^m\), whence
-  \[
-    \mathrm{Prec}_m
-    \le\frac{\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}}{a_m(\mathcal A)}
-    \le\frac{2B_b}{c_r}\frac1m,
-  \]
-  and
-  \[
-    \abs{(L(\mathcal A)\cap\Sigma_b^m)\triangle\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}
-    \ge a_m(\mathcal A)-\abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}
-    \ge \frac{c_r}{4}b^m.
-  \]
-  This proves the positive-density lower bound.
-
-  Taking
-  \(M_{\mathcal A,b}:=\max_r M_r\) and the minimum over the finitely many
-  positive constants \(A_b/2\) and \(c_r/4\) appearing above gives the
-  final all-large-\(m\) constant after replacing \(c_r b^m/4\) by the
-  weaker \(c_r b^m/(4m)\) in the positive-density residue classes.
-  The output statement follows from strongly connected component and
-  period algorithms, exact rational linear algebra, root isolation for
-  the finitely many characteristic polynomials, and the certified
-  resolvent construction in \Cref{lem:effective-spectral-constants}.
-  The certificate is compressed by recurrent class and cyclic class.
-  Printing all residues, and taking the final minimum by enumeration,
-  are charged to the chosen output representation.
-\end{proof}

-\begin{example}[Two explicit certificates]
-  \label{ex:base-ending-zero-certificate}
-  Let \(\mathcal A_0\) be the complete DFA over \(\Sigma_b\) accepting
-  exactly the non-empty words ending in \(0\). It has states
-  \(q_0,q_1\), initial state \(q_0\), accepting set \(\{q_1\}\), and
-  transitions
-  \[
-    \delta(q_i,0)=q_1,\qquad
-    \delta(q_i,d)=q_0\quad(1\le d\le b-1).

-  \[
-    B=\begin{pmatrix} b-1&1\\ b-1&1\end{pmatrix},

-    P=\begin{pmatrix} (b-1)/b&1/b\\ (b-1)/b&1/b\end{pmatrix}.

-    c_0=\pi_{1,0}(\{q_1\})=1/b.
-  \]
-  Since \(P^2=P\), one may take \(S_0=P\), \(N_0=1\), any rational
-  \(0<\tau_0<\theta_0<1\), and any rational \(K_0>0\) for the advertised
-  convergence estimate on all \(m\ge1\). Equivalently,
-  \(a_m(\mathcal A_0)=b^{m-1}\) and
-  \(a_m(\mathcal A_0)/b^m=1/b\) for every \(m\ge1\).
-
-  Let \(A_b,B_b,M_b\) be the constants from
-  \Cref{lem:base-prime-count}. The positive-density branch of
-  \Cref{thm:effective-fixed-dfa-prime-obstruction} may therefore use the

-  \[
-    M_0:=\left\lceil\max\{M_b,4bB_b\}\right\rceil .

-    \le

-    \le
-    \frac{bB_b}{m},

-  \[
-    \abs{(L(\mathcal A_0)\cap\Sigma_b^m)\triangle\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}

-    \ge
-    \frac{1}{2b}b^m .
-  \]
-  Thus the certificate has \(D_A=1\), \(c_0=1/b\), precision constant

-    \abs{\mathcal P_m^{(b)}}

-    A_b\frac{b^m}{m}.
-  \]
